ing: 400 g sifted icing sugar, for dusting
small drop of red or pink food colouring
st: Pre-heat the oven to 180Â°c and line a 20cm square cake pan and a 20cm round cake pan with baking paper.
Mix the chocolate cake according to packet instructions (add 3 large eggs, 250 ml oil and 250 ml hot water).
Transfer the batter to the prepared cake pans then place in the oven.
Allow to bake for 25-30 minutes or until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Remove the cakes from the oven and allow to cool completely.
To make the buttercream, whip the butter until light and fluffy then add the icing sugar and mix until well combined.
Add a little of the milk if the buttercream is too thick then add the pink food colouring and mix until you have the desired shade.
When the cakes are cool, half the round cake and place the two halves on two of the sides of the square cake, to form a heart.
Generously spread the buttercream over the cake to cover.
Top with raspberries and dust with icing sugar before serving.

t: Hot cross buns with spiced honey butter
ing: 500 g cake flour, plus extra for dusting
st: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar, spices and salt in a bowl and mix until combined.
In a measuring jug, whisk together the melted butter, eggs and milk then pour into the dry ingredients.
Mix until a sticky, soft dough forms. Turn out onto a floured surface and knead for 5 minutes.
Place the dough into a bowl and cover with clingfilm or a damp cloth then allow to rise for 1 hour.
When the dough has risen, remove from the bowl and knead in the raisins. Return to the bowl, cover and allow to rise for another 30 minutes.
Pre-heat the oven to 180Â°c and line a large baking tray with baking paper.

Form dough balls roughly the size of golf balls out of the risen dough and place in a circular pattern on the prepared baking tray. Mix together 5 tbls of flour and 3-4 tbls of water and pipe crosses onto the buns.
Allow to rise for another 30 minutes then place in the pre-heated oven.
Allow to bake for 25-30 minutes until the hot cross buns are golden brown and cooked through.
While the buns are baking, combine 1/2 cup of water and 1/2 cup of sugar to make the glaze in a small saucepan and allow to come to a boil.
When the buns have baked, remove them from the oven and immediately brush the glaze over the top.
Allow to cool slightly.
For the spiced honey butter, simply beat together 150 g butter, 3 tbls of honey and 1/2 tsp of ground cinnamon then serve with the warm hot cross buns.

t: Hot cross beef burgers with spicy slaw
ing: 3 tbsp canola oil, plus extra for greasing
st: Break up the burger patties and mould into six smaller ones. Heat the oil in a pan over a high heat and cook the patties for 2 minutes on one side, or until browned. Reduce the heat to medium, then cook the other side for another 3 minutes.
Remove the patties from the pan and allow them to rest for 2 minutes, then coat them in the spicy Korean BBQ marinade.
Heat the butter in the same pan, halve the hot cross buns through the middle and toast in the pan, cut side down, over a medium heat for 45 seconds, or until golden.
To make the slaw, combine the shredded lettuce, 1 cup of mayonnaise and 1 teaspoon of chilli paste.
Place a spoonful of spicy slaw on the base of each hot cross bun, then top with a patty.
Top with a slice of smoked provolone and the top of the bun

ing: 60 g sesame seeds, plus extra for sprinkling
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Grease and line a 22 cm round springform cake tin. Cream the butter and caster sugar together until well combined.

Add the eggs one at a time, beating each one into the mixture until combined. Fold the flour into the mixture with the baking powder, salt and lemon zest. Gently mix in the sesame seeds and 150 g blueberries to incorporate evenly.

Pour the batter into the cake tin, smooth the surface with a spatula and sprinkle over the remaining blueberries and extra sesame seeds. Bake for 25â30 minutes. Remove from the oven and allow to cool.

To make the icing, combine the icing sugar and lemon juice. Add a splash of hot water if the icing is too stiff. Drizzle over the cake just before serving and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds if you like.

ing: sea salt and pepper to taste
st: In a large bowl, combine the lamb with: 1 teaspoon of toasted & crushed cumin seeds, fennel seeds and coriander seeds, 2 teaspoons of mother-in-law spice mix, 1 teaspoon of tumeric, 1 cinnamon quill, 1 teaspoon of salt and 2-3 tablespoons oil and allow to marinate for at least 1 hour but ideally overnight.

Heat a large pot over high heat and add the oil. Fry the onions until soft and translucent then add the garlic, 1 teaspoon of: ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and mother-in-law spice mix and allow to fry for another minute.
Add the marinated meat and allow to cook for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, stock and sugar then lower the heat and allow to simmer gently, covered, for 90 minutes.
After 90 minutes, uncover the pot and allow to simmer for another 60-90 minutes until the lamb is soft and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Season to taste then serve.

ing: 1/2 lemon, cut into 8 slices for garnishing
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
400 g woolworths calamari tubes and tentacles
st: Place the lemon zest and juice, 2 T olive oil, chilli and mint in a bowl and season to taste. Mix and set aside.
Toss the calamari with 2 cloves crushed garlic and the remaining olive oil, then pan-fry in small batches over a high heat for 3â4 minutes until pink and cooked through.
Toss the calamari with the baby leaves and dressing.
Pan-fry the sliced baguette in the pan for 2 minutes, or until golden.
Halve the remaining garlic cloves and rub onto the baguette while itâs sill hot.
Serve the calamari with the bruschetta.

ing: 1 cup Vinagre De Jerez Sherry Vinegar
100 g Hazelnuts, blanched, roasted and roughly chopped
3/4 cup sugar for the egg whites
st: Preheat the oven to 180 Â°C.
For the pickled beetroot, wash the beetroot and place 8-10 beetroots on a large piece of foil.
Drizzle with olive oil and seal the foil on all sides to make a parcel.
Repeat with the remaining beetroot.
Place the parcels on two roasting trays and roast for 45 minutes â 1 hour or until tender.
Allow to cool slightly, then peel the beetroots and cut each one into 8 wedges.
Combine the sherry vinegar, sugar and3/4cup of water in a saucepan and bring to the boil, stirring until the sugar has dissolved.
Add the beetroot to the pickling liquid and allow to cool.
Dress the baby leaves and wild rocket with olive oil.
To serve, arrange the beetroots on a large platter. Sprinkle with the leaves, chunks of Gorgonzola and roasted hazelnuts. Drizzle with olive oil, balsamic vinegar and season.

ing: extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
1/4 cup panko bread crumbs or dried bread crumbs
st: Begin by preheating a frying to a medium heat.
Mix the panko bread crumbs, salt, extra virgin olive oil and a dash of Deltino Anchovy Essence together, and add the mixture to the pan.
Toss the mixture constantly to ensure that the bread crumb mixture is cooked evenly and does not burn.
Once the bread crumbs are a deep golden colour, remove from the pan and set aside.
Next, bring a heavily salted pot of water to boil and blanch the kale for 2 minutes and remove from the pot of water, whilst retaining the water in the pot.
Using the water, cook the pasta until âalâdenteâ, and then drain and set aside.
Whilst the pasta is boiling, heat oil in a large skillet, add the chilli, crushed garlic, a pinch of salt and toast until golden.
Then add he kale and sautÃ© for 2 minutes until the kale is well coated with the oil.
Add the drained pasta, ricotta and the rest of the Deltino Anchovy Essence and toss well on a low heat for half a minute.
Add more salt if necessary, black pepper and top off with your toasted breadcrumbs *and a dash of extra virgin olive oil.

ing: 180 g Delizie Di Calabria garlic, oil & hot pepper condiment
st: Cook the spaghetti in a large saucepan of salted boiling water according to the packet instructions.

About 4 minutes before the pasta is ready, heat 100g of garlic, oil, toasted bread crumbs and Calabria hot pepper condiment in a large frying pan and sautÃ© the garlic and chilli. Add Â½ cup of hot pasta water to stop the cooking any further. Remove from the heat while you drain the pasta.
Return the pan to high heat and add the pasta, parsley and a little more olive oil. Keep tossing the pasta. The pasta water and oil will emulsify thickening and coating the spaghetti.

t: Leg of lamb with sweet potatoes
ing: 1 large bulb garlic, sectioned and peeled
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Place the garlic cloves onto a baking tray and drizzle lightly with olive oil. Roast for 20 minutes, or until tender and fragrant. Remove from the oven and set aside.
Combine 1 cup of the yoghurt with the tikka masala paste.
Transfer the lamb to a large bowl and rub the tikka-yoghurt marinade onto the meat. Leave to marinate for an hour.
Toss the sweet potato halves with a drizzle of olive oil and sprinkle with chilli salt, to taste.
Together with the leg of lamb, place on a hot grid over smouldering coals and grill for 25 minutes, or until the meat is cooked to your preference.
Remove and allow the meat to rest for 5 minutes before carving.
Add the coriander, remaining Â½ cup olive oil and the lemon juice to a blender and blitz to combine.
Toss the sweet potatoes through half of the coriander pesto and arrange on a platter, along with the slices of lamb and roasted garlic cloves.
Combine the remaining coriander pesto with the last cup of yoghurt and spoon over the lamb and potatoes.

ing: 140 g flour, plus extra for dusting
st: To prepare the grated zucchini, mix it with salt and allow it to drain in a colander for 20 minutes.
Place the zucchini in a tea towel and squeeze out as much of the liquid as possible.
Mix the zucchini, basil, lemon, ricotta, egg yolks and Pecorino cheese, then add half the flour to form a dough that is not too sticky to work with.
Add more flour if needed.
Divide the dough and roll the two halves in the rest of the flour, creating two 2 1/2 cm thick rolls.
Slice the rolls into 2 1/2 cm wide pieces then gently create ridges in them either with a gnocchi board or using a floured fork.
Cook the gnocchi in boiling water until it floats. Remove and drain.
Toss the gnocchi in a bowl with the butter, basil leaves and pine nuts.
Serve warm with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

ing: 50 g castor sugar, plus extra for dipping the pastry shapes
st: Scoop the mascarpone into a large pan with the castor sugar.
Stir to melt the sugar over a low heat, then simmer for 1 minute.
Take the pan off the heat, add the lemon juice and zest and whisk well.
Pour into 6 ramekins and refrigerate for 12 hours.
Sprinkle with extra lemon zest before serving.

ing: 2 cups flour, plus extra for dusting
st: Preheat the oven to 175 Â°C.
Lightly grease a 22 cm springform pan.
In a medium sized bowl, mix the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt, and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the buttermilk, lemon juice, lemon zest and vanilla extract, and set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, beat the eggs and granulated sugar for about 5 minutes at high speed until pale and fluffy.
Lower the speed to medium-high, and drizzle in the olive oil slowly, mixing until well incorporated.
With the mixer on low, add half the flour mixture until well incorporated.
Add the buttermilk mixture next, then the remaining flour mixture, until just blended.
Fold in the almonds.
Scrape the batter into the prepared springform pan and bake at 175 Â°C for 40 â 45 minutes, or until the top is golden and a toothpick inserted near the centre comes out clean.
Let the cake cool in the pan on a wire rack for 20 minutes, then carefully remove the pan sides. Allow the cake to cool completely.
Drizzle with honey or dust with icing sugar and cut into slices to serve.

ing: 1 juiced and zested lemon, cut into 8 slices
2 kg free range leg of lamb
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
2 large handfuls Italian parsley, leaves picked from stalks and finely chopped
st: Preheat the oven to 200 Â°C.
For the lamb marinade, mix the crushed garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice and 60 ml of olive oil.
Rub the marinade over the lamb and season.
Place the lamb on a rack that fits in a roasting tray and roast for 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours.
When done, remove the lamb and rest, covered loosely with foil for 15 minutes before carving.
For the potatoes, boil them for 10 minutes, then drain and scuff the edges. Allow to stand to release steam for a few minutes.
Put 80 ml of olive oil in a large roasting pan and put it in the oven for 5 minutes to get hot. Carefully add the potatoes, season with salt and black pepper and return the pan to the oven.
Roast the potatoes for about 1 1/4 hours until they are crisp and golden, tossing them in the hot oil occasionally during cooking.
To make the gremolata, combine the chopped parsley, crushed garlic, lemon juice and lemon zest.
Carve the lamb and season if needed.
Serve slices of the lamb and roast potatoes on a large, warmed platter and sprinkle with gremolata.

ing: 50 g castor sugar, plus extra for dipping the pastry shapes
st: Scoop the mascarpone into a large pan with the castor sugar.
Stir to melt the sugar over a low heat, then simmer for 1 minute.
Take the pan off the heat, add the lemon juice and zest and whisk well.
Pour into 6 ramekins and refrigerate for 12 hours.
Sprinkle with extra lemon zest before serving.

ing: 1 1/2  cups Cheddar cheese, grated + extra for serving
200 g Dry Cured Wood Smoked Streaky Bacon
st: Preheat the oven to 180âc and grease a loaf tin.
Mix the yeast, sugar and a little of the water and set aside for 5mins.
Place the flour in a large bowl with the salt and make a well in the middle.
Pour in the yeast mixture which should now be frothy and bubbling slightly and the remaining water and mix until combined. Add a little extra water if the dough feels very dry.
Turn the dough out onto a clean surface and knead for 10mins until the dough is smooth.
Place in an oiled bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Leave in a warm area of the kitchen for roughly an 1hr or until doubled in size.
While the dough rises, lay the bacon on a wire rack and place onto a baking tray.
Brush maple syrup on each strip and then place in the oven until crispy and sticky. Continue to brush maple syrup every 10mins until the bacon is done. Roughly break the bacon into smaller pieces.
Flash fry the sage leaves in a hot pan with a little oil. Place on kitchen paper to soak excess oil and set aside.
Once the dough has risen, knock back the dough and turn out onto a clean table. Cut the dough into 2 and roll out into rectangles and then trim to straighten the edges.
Spread melted butter onto the surface of the dough and sprinkle with cheese, torn crispy sage leaves and Â½ the bacon.
Cut the dough into squares the same size as your loaf tin.
Transfer the layers to your greased loaf tin. I find it easier to hold the loaf tin up while stacking the squares on top of each other.
Sprinkle with extra cheese, cover with plastic wrap and allow to rise for 30mins.
Place in the preheated oven and bake for 45-55mins until golden brown.
Remove from the oven when it is ready and allow to cool for 10mins before serving with lots of butter and extra cheese and sticky maple bacon.

ing: 1 Tbsp sea salt, plus extra to taste
st: For the caramel sauce, melt the butter in a pan over medium heat. Add the brown sugar and stir until the sugar has dissovled and the mixture is creamy. Remove from heat.
Slowly stir in the whipping cream and salt with a wooden spoon and set aside. The mixture will bubble.
In a bowl, toss the apple slices with lemon juice, cinnamon and nutmeg.
In another pan, melt 1 tablespoon of butter over a medium heat.
Add the apple slices and cook them, uncovered, for 4 to 6 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally. Add the soaked raisins and 1/4 of the caramel sauce.
Heat the pancakes by placing one pancake at a time on a microwavable plate and heat on full power (Cat E/800W) for 30 seconds.
Place the pancakes browned side down on warmed plates. Top one side of the pancakes with the apple mixture and fold them half over so that the browned sides are visible.
Drizzle the pancakes and apples with the remaining caramel sauce and top with the pecans and a sprinkling of sea salt flakes.
Toss cubed pork fillet in the crushed garlic, honey and olive oil and marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil (sunflower, peanut or canola) and fry the pork for 5 minutes, or until cooked through.
Top with chopped fresh red chillies.

ing: Italian parsley finely chopped, for sprinkling
1 x 400 g can Chickpeas, drained and rinsed
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Rinse and drain the lentils. Heat 3 T olive oil in a pan and gently soften the onion, celery and carrot.
Stir in the garlic and cumin. Add the lentils and stock. Bring to a bubble, then reduce the heat and simmer for 40 minutes, or until the lentils are very soft. Season to taste.
Meanwhile, brown the lamb meatballs in the remaining olive oil over a medium heat for a few minutes on each side side until just cooked.
Drain well on kitchen paper.
Add the chickpeas and browned meatballs to the lentils and heat through. Sprinkle with parsley. Pass around the lemon wedges at the table.

ing: 1 x 400 g can Tomato and onion mix
6 Extra large free range egg whites
500 g cake flour, plus extra for dusting
st: Preheat the oven to 230Â°C.
Blend the eggs, milk, water, flour and salt. Chill while you cook the boerewors.
Grease a 25 x 18 x 2.5 cm baking pan. Cut the boerewors to fit the pan and add a few sprigs of rosemary. Bake for 10 minutes, or until the boerewors starts to colour.
If necessary, whisk the batter. Pour over the boerewors and bake for a further 15 minutes, or until puffed and golden.
Serve with the tomato-and-onion sauce.

ing: Blue Elephant Thai jasmine rice, cooked
180 g Extra fine green beans, roughly chopped
1 x 400 g can Woolworths coconut cream
400 g Free range chicken mini breast fillets
2 thumb sized pieces fresh ginger, grated
1/2 cup medium red onions, thinly sliced
40 g desiccated coconut + extra for sprinkling
st: Marinate the chicken in the coconut cream for 30 minutes. While this marinates mix the breadcrumbs, coconut, chilli flakes and Thai 7 blend spice.
Remove the chicken from the coconut cream and allow excess liquid to drip off. Dip each piece of chicken into the breadcrumb mixture and set aside ready to pan fry.

Place the chicken pieces in a med-high heated frying pan with a little oil until cooked through and golden. Be careful not to overcrowd the pan and rather fry in batches. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

In the same pan, fry the red onions, garlic and ginger until the onions have softened. Add the sweetcorn, green beans and peas and cook for a further 2 minutes. Add the cooked rice and mix together with the other vegetables.
Using a spatula make a space in the pan to fry the egg. Crack the eggs into the space and scramble the eggs until dry, try not mix the egg with the other ingredients in the pan at this stage.
Once the egg is completely cooked mix thoroughly with the rest of the vegetables and rice.
Spoon the fried rice onto a large plate.
Lastly flash fry the Swiss Chard in the same pan heated high with a tablespoon of soy sauce or tamari and serve on the top of the rice.

ing: 350 g Easy to Wok Calamari Tubes & Tentacles
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Place the lemon zest and juice, 2 T olive oil, Chilli and mint in a bowl and season to taste. Mix and set aside.

Toss the calamari with 2 cloves crushed garlic and the remaining olive oil, then pan-fry in small batches over a high heat for 3â4 minutes until pink and cooked through. Toss the calamari with the baby leaves and dressing.
Pan-fry the sliced baguette in the pan for 2 minutes, or until golden. Halve the remaining garlic cloves and rub onto the baguette while itâs still hot.
Serve the calamari with the bruschetta.
Mix the spices, salt and pepper and rub into the chicken to season evenly and leave covered in the fridge overnight.

Heat the oil in a deep-sided pot on a medium heat while you prepare the chicken. If you have a thermometer â heat to 160âc. Mix the flour, spices and salt and pepper together to evenly combine. Pour the buttermilk in another bowl. Dip the chicken into the flour mix and then into the buttermilk. Repeat the process to form a double coating and ultimately a thicker, crispier coating when fried.

Test the oil is ready by dropping a little of the coating from the chicken into the oil and it should sizzle. Fry the chicken in batches in order to ensure the pot is not overcrowded.  Fry until golden brown, roughly 12 â 15mins. Place the fried chicken onto paper towel to soak up excess oil. Serve the fried chicken with spicy buttermilk dipping sauce.
To make the sauce, combine all the ingredients and mix until smooth.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°.

Fry the onion in a little oil until softened. Add the garlic and mince and fry until evenly cooked and crumbly. Add the carrots, raisins, sultanas and spices and fry a little longer until the carrots have softened slightly. Remove from the heat and allow to cool.

While the mince cools, soak the bread in the milk and set aside for 5 minutes. Lightly squeeze the bread and mash with a fork. Whisk the eggs and add to the mashed bread. Mix the egg mixture into the cooled mince. Spoon the mixture into an ovenproof dish and spread evenly.
Mix the cream and eggs together for the topping and pour over the mince. Top with bay leaves and bake for 30-40 minutes until firm and golden brown.
Prepare 1 x 80 g packet Woolworths strawberry-flavoured jelly according to package instructions, using pink Champagne instead of cold water.
Pour into a shallow bowl, add a handful of gooseberries, then chill.

ing: 150 g Double Cream Coconut & Lime Flavoured Yoghurt
st: Line each hole of a 6-hole muffin pan with plastic wrap, allowing a 2 cm overhang on each hole.
To make the bases, combine the crushed cookies with the butter and mix well.
Divide the biscuit mixture into the 6 holes of the muffin pan and press down to ensure the bases are firm and compact.
For the cheesecake mixture, place the boiling water in a heatproof jug and sprinkle the gelatine over it. Stir to dissolve.
Using an electric mixer, beat the cream cheese and castor sugar until smooth.
Add the yoghurt, coconut cream, lime zest and lime juice and mix well to combine. Add the gelatine mixture and mix again until smooth.
Pour the cream cheese micture onto the cookie bases. Cover and refrigerate for 6 hours or until firm.
Use the overhanging plastic wrap to lift the cheesecakes from the muffin pan.
Remove the plastic wrap and serve the cheesecakes topped with toasted coconut shavings and fresh mint leaves.

ing: 1 x 75  g bag Woolworths Asian Chinese Prawn Crackers
4 Free-range chicken breasts , cut into large chunks
300 g sugar for the egg whites
1 Spring onion, thinly sliced, to garnish
4 Tbsp canola oil, plus extra for greasing
st: Heat half the oil in a wok over a high heat. Cook the chicken in batches until sealed and golden brown. Remove from the wok and set aside.
To make the glaze, place all the ingredients in the wok and cook, stirring, until the sugar has just dissolved.
Return the chicken to the wok and toss to coat in the glaze. Cook until the chicken is cooked through. Serve immediately with the prawn crackers and beetroot onion pickle. Garnish with spring onion.
To make the beetroot onion pickle, heat the white wine vinegar, sugar and salt in a saucepan over a medium heat until the sugar has dissolved. Pour over the beetroot and onion and set aside to cool.

ing: 600 g Woolworths lightly smoked rainbow trout fillets
1 x 10 cm piece ginger piece, peeled and roughly chopped
st: To make the rice, pound the lemongrass and ginger into a coarse paste using a pestle and mortar. Transfer to a saucepan and add the rice, salt, chicken stock and water. Cook according to package instructions.
Place the trout, skin side down, in a pan over a high heat and cook until the skin is golden and crisp.

Serve with the rice and drizzle over the soya sauce. Place the sliced spring onion in iced water for a few minutes until it curls. Garnish with the spring onion, chilli, basil leaves and squeeze over the limes.

ing: 1.5 kg  Easy to Cook Lamb Shoulder Roast, cooked and pulled into large chunks
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
60 g Butter, melted plus extra for frying
4 Tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
st: Remove the meat from bone and set aside. Heat the oil over a medium heat then add the onions to the pan. Allow the onions to cook down slowly and caramelize until completely soft and golden brown.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute before adding the spices. Continue cooking until the spices become fragrant and toasted. Add the bay leaf, celery leaves and parsley and stir through.
Pour in the demi-glace and water and stir into the dish along with the lemon zest and sumac. Add the torn lamb and set aside.
For the topping: Melt together the butter, garlic and sumac. Season with salt to taste. Begin layering the potatoes over the lamb dish drizzling some of the sumac butter over each layer of potato.
Place the dish layered with the potatoes in an oven preheated to 180Â°C to cook for 35-45 minutes or until the potato is cooked and golden on top.

ing: 1 Free range egg, lightly beaten with a little milk
st: In a hot pan over a medium heat, gently fry onion in olive oil, until softened. Combine with beef mince, parsley, clove garlic, korma paste, beaten  egg and seasoning, to taste.
Bring together the mixture and mould into patties. In a pan over a medium to high heat, fry the patties in hot olive oil, until cooked through.
Grate pineapple with cucumber, then fold through cups plain yoghurt.
Serve the patties and pineapple raita on toasted ciabatta with lettuce leaves.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Mix 150 g softened butter with 2 t chopped sage, 1 T chopped Italian parsley, 2 t chopped chives, 1 t chopped oregano and season to taste.
Spread onto sliced baguettes and bake in tinfoil for 5 minutes, or until warmed through.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Sift the flour and salt. Add the buttermilk and mix until you have a sticky dough. Add one of the extra options.
Line a medium-sized loaf tin or 23 cm cake tin with baking paper that you have either buttered or sprayed with cooking spray, then pour in the mixture.
Bake for 45 minutes to an hour, or until a skewer comes out clean.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
85 g almonds, toasted, plus extra to garnish
120 g dried apricots, dried and chopped
120 g prunes, pitted and coarsley chopped
salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Make the stuffing a day in advance and refrigerate. Melt the butter in a large pan and add the onion. Cook gently, for about 5 minutes, or until softened but still pale. Add the pork and veal, and stir with a large fork until it changes colour, losing its pinkness.
Remove from the heat and mix with the ham and liver. Allow to cool. Lightly toss the breadcrumbs, spices, fruit, nuts, egg, sherry and seasoning. Mix well with the meats.

ing: 600 g Lightly smoked rainbow trout, skin on, scored
extra virgin olive oil, for drizzling
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Arrange the hot-smoked trout and melon on plates.
Poach the eggs and place each egg onto the melon on each plate.
Top with a handful of wild rocket, a squeeze of lemon juice, a drizzle of olive oil and season to taste.

ing: 2 gelatine leaves, soaked in cold water for 10 minutes
st: Scoop out the granadilla flesh and combine with the honey liqueur.

Soften the gelatine leaves in cool water for 5 minutes and squeeze out any excess liquid. Add a tablespoon of hot water to dissolve, then combine with the granadilla mixture and pour into individual trifle moulds.
Chill until set.

ing: 8-12 florets tenderstem broccoli, sautÃ©ed or blanched
st: Preheat the oven to 220 Â°C.
Season the duck with salt and place it in a roasting pan.
Roast the duck for 10 minutes, then turn the heat down to 180 Â°C and cook it for a further 50 â 55 minutes, basting with the honey every 15 minutes.
To make the sauce, combine the orange juice and zest, cherries, wine, sugar, ginger, cinnamon and cloves in a medium saucepan.
Stir the ingredients over a medium heat until the sugar dissolves and the mixture comes to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered for about 20 minutes, stirring frequently, until the cherries burst and the juices thicken slightly.
Transfer the sauce to a bowl and set aside.
Serve the duck and cherry sauce warm with the sautÃ©ed tenderstem broccoli.

t: Hot smoked salmon and beetroot salad
ing: 1/2 head broccoli, rinsed, cut into small florets and blanched
2 bulbs Candy striped beetroot, scrubbed and thinly sliced
1 Mediterranean cucumber, halved and sliced diagonally
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: To make the salad dressing, crush the blackberries in a bowl with a fork and add the red wine vinegar, maple syrup and olive oil. Season, mix well and set aside.
For the salad, arrange the rocket leaves, chicory, cucumber, spring onion, sliced beetroot and blanched romanesco broccoli florets on a large plate or platter.
Place the salmon, whole or flaked, over the salad, together with the micro leaves and blackberries.
Serve the salad with the dressing drizzled over it or on the side.
Place the ice cream in a large mixing bowl and stir to soften slightly. Spoon 3 cups into a 20 cm springform cake tin and top with the raspberries, reserving a few to garnish.
Repeat the process with the remaining ice cream, blueberries and strawberries.
Spoon the last of the ice cream over the strawberries and freeze overnight.
To unmould, wrap a warm, damp dishcloth around the tin and run a hot palette knife around the edge of the cake to loosen. Release the springform tin and remove.
Garnish with the remaining berries and slice using a hot knife to serve.

ing: Norwegian Salmon Poached Lemon & Pink Peppercorn
st: Sign in/Register

ing: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Carefully scoop out the flesh from the potatoes leaving the skin behind like a shell.
Mix the potato flesh with the gammon or bacon, spring onions, chives, crÃ¨me fraÃ®che and seasoning.
Spoon the mixture back into the potato shells and top with the grated cheese. Bake for 15 minutes, or until golden. Serve hot with rocket and baby tomatoes or cold on the road the next day.

ing: 1 packed cup micro herbs, for serving
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve until the water runs clear. Bring 3 cups water to a boil in a suitable saucepan. Add Â½ t salt and the rinsed and drained quinoa.

Bring back to a boil, reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the quinoa is tender and translucent and the germ separates from the seed. The germ will look like a tiny curl. Drain and return to the pan. Cover the pan with a clean tea towel and replace the lid. Leave for 10 minutes, then fluff up using a large fork.
Meanwhile, finely chop the herbs, then mix with the quinoa. Moisten with lemon juice and olive oil and season to taste. Serve at room temperature.
Place the raspberries and caster sugar in a small saucepan with 2â3 cup water. Bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove from the heat and strain through a sieve.
Pour the mixture into a container and place in the freezer. Scrape the mixture with a fork every hour to form soft flakes.

Mix the coffee and hot chocolate or cocoa with 2 cups boiling water. Pour into a large, shallow container and allow to cool. Place in the freezer and scrape the mixture with a fork every hour to form soft flakes.

Just before serving, fluff up both granitas using a fork. Decant the raspberry and mocha granitas into separate tall glasses and place on the table with shot glasses into which the granitas can be layered and served immediately.

t: Incir Tathsi Figs stuffed with walnuts
ing: 1 cup Tea made with bay leaves, lemon juice, cloves, sugar and water to taste
60 g Walnuts, coarsley chopped, plus extra for grating
st: Pour the boiling water over the figs and soak for 2 hours. Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Hold the figs by their stalks and make a small incision in the soft end of each fig. Stuff the walnuts into the figs and place in an ovenproof dish, with the stalks facing upwards.

Simmer the tea, honey or sugar and lemon zest for 10 minutes. Sweeten the syrup to taste with more honey or sugar. Pour the syrup over the figs and bake for 20 minutes. Serve hot or cold garnished with pomegranate rubies and grate over extra walnuts.

Place chopped dates and figs in a blender and blend for 2-3 minutes (1-2 tablespoon of water can be added if necessary). You will need to use a greased spatula to remove the date and fig mixture from the blender jug.
Dry-roast the nuts in a pan on medium heat for about 3-4 minutes, and remove from pan. Using the same pan, dry-roast the sesame seeds and coconut for about a minute.
Heat the ghee or butter in a heavy-based pot. Add the date and fig mixture and sautÃ© for approximately 5 minutes on medium heat.
Now add the chopped nut, sesame seeds, desiccated coconut and cardamom powder and allow to cook till the mixture comes together, resembling a dough-like substance.
Remove from the heat and allow to cool before kneading the mixture.
Grease your palms with some ghee and roll into ping pong sized balls. Roll in powdered edible glitter and allow to dry for a couple of hours before storing in an airtight container.
Alternatively you can roll the mixture into a log shape, and sprinkle with powdered almonds and pistachios. Wrap in cling wrap and refrigerate for a couple of hours before slicing and serving.

ing: 220 g Woolworths soft-eating sundried Turkish figs, roughly chopped
75 g good quality dark chocolate, roughly chopped
st: Preheat the oven to 160Â°C.

Lightly grease 1 x 24-cm springform baking tin, then line the base with baking paper. Sift the flour, cocoa, bicarbonate of soda and spices into a large bowl. Add the figs, chocolate, citrus zests and hazelnuts, then, using your hands, rub the chopped ingredients through the dry ingredients to distribute evenly.
Place the wine, sugar, butter and honey in a small saucepan over a medium heat for 5 minutes, or until the sugar dissolves and the butter melts. Remove from the heat, then cool for 10 minutes.
Make a well in the flour mixture, add the honey mixture and stir until well combined. Spoon the mixture into the baking tin and smooth the top evenly.

Bake for 1 hour or until a skewer inserted comes out with large crumbs attached (it will still be a little sticky in the middle). Cool in the tin for 10 minutes. Remove the cake from the tin and serve sprinkled with the golden almonds.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Soak bamboo or wood skewers in water for half an hour to prevent them from burning during grilling.

Slice the sausage into chunks. Mix the mushrooms, tomatoes and onion with the olive oil and a little seasoning. Thread the sausage, mushrooms, tomatoes, onion and rosemary sprigs onto the soaked skewers.
Grill for 4 minutes on each side until the sausage is browned, just cooked and still moist.
Serve with the potato and watercress salad.
Remove 6 kale leaves from their stems and blend with 30 g basil, 25 g hazelnuts, 25 g almonds, 100 g finely grated hard cheese, 2 cloves garlic, 2 T lemon juice and 1 cup olive oil.
Season to taste.

ing: 18 Small lamb cutlets, brushed with olive oil and seasoned
300 g Basmati rice, rinsed in cold water
st: To make the pilaf, heat the oil in a medium saucepan.
Add the onion and cook for 3 â 4 minutes or until lightly browned.
Add the spices and cook for another 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the rice, coat it well in the oil and spice mixture and cook for a few seconds or until slightly translucent.
Add the vegetable or chicken stock and coconut milk and bring to the boil.
Cover the pot and reduce the heat to a gentle simmer. Leave to cook for a further 12 â 15 minutes or until the rice is tender.
Remove from the heat and add the pistachios, desiccated coconut, mint, coriander and a squeeze of lime to the rice. Season to taste and set aside with the lid on.
Heat the grill to high and cook the lamb cutlets for a few minutes on each side.
Serve the pilaf with the lamb cutlets and lime wedges.

ing: 1 Vanilla pod, split and seeds scraped out
st: Preheat the oven to 170C
Bring the whipping cream to the boil over a medium heat with the lime leaves and vanilla seeds.
Simmer over a low heat for 2-3 minutes, then remove from the heat and allow to infuse for 10 minutes.
Whisk half the castor sugar and the egg yolks until pale and thick.
Add the lime zest and juice, then whisk into the cream mixture.
Strain the cream micture, discarding the solids.
Ladle the mixture into six ramekins or ovenproof dishes, place them in a roasting pan and pour enough boiling water into the pan to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Cover loosely with foil and bake for 30 minutes, or until just set with a slight wobble in the centre.
Remove the rameklins from the pan, allow to cool for 30 minutes, then chill for 2 hours.
Sprinkle the tops with the remaining castor sugar and caramelise it using a kitchen blowtorch, or placing it under a hot grill for 1-2 minutes, ensuring that the sugar doesn't burn.
Serve topped with lime zest and lime slices
Heat the olive oil in a pan over a medium-high heat.
Add the pork steaks and cook, turning occasionally for 5 minutes or until browned. Transfer to a plate.
Add the ginger, garlic, star anise, soy sauce, Sweet Indonesian Soy Sauce, honey and lime juice to the pan and bring to the boil over a high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 5-7 minutes or until the sauce has thickened.
Please the pork steaks back in the pan, turning to coat them in sauce.
Serve the pork with the sauce, sauteed bok choy and lime slices.
Combine the pineapple juice, coconut water, sugar and lime juice in a large pitcher and stir until the sugar has dissolved.
Add sparkling water to taste and serve over ice, garnished with slices of lime and mint leaves.

t: Lime, feta and chilli grilled corn
ing: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Preheat a grill pan on high.
Place the sweetcorn on the grill pan, cover and cook, turning for approximately 10 minutes until the husks are charred.
Using a kicthen towel, pull back the husks and place the sweetcorn back on the grill pan with the husks away from the heat.
Cover and cook, turning for about 10-15 minutes, until the sweetcorn kernels are partially charred.
Combine the mayonnaise, lime juice and cayenne pepper and brush over the cooked corn.
Top the sweetcorn with the finely crumbled feat cheese, season with sea salt and black pepper and serve with lime wedges.

t: Lime, mango and ginger cookie sundaes
ing: mangoes (750g), peeled and cut in small cubes
st: Remove the flesh from two mangoes and puree in a blender
Peel and cube the reminaing mangoes.
Mix the lime zest and lime juice, vanilla seeds, icing sugar, yoghurt and whipping cream together.
To assemble the sandaes, divide half of the mango puree into 4 glasses and top each with the yoghurt mixture.
Sprinkle half of the crushed ginger cookies on top of the yoghurt micture, then top with the remaining puree.
Place the cubed mango on the puree, then top with the remaining crushed ginger cookies.
Place the sundaes in the fridge to set for 30 minutes.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
A small handful coriander, finely chopped
A handful torn fresh mint leaves
4 portions of fresh salmon fillet (150g â 200g each)
1 tsp ginger, finely chopped or grated
st: In a glass bowl, combine the lime juice, jalapeno pepper, ginger and olive oil.
Add the diced salmon and toss together.
Cover with plastic and chill ofr 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until the fish has started to go pale.
Add the remaining ingredients, season with salt and pepper and stir to combine.
Serve with lime wedges.

t: Lamb chops with lime, cumin and cardamom
ing: A handful Pomegranate rubies, to serve
freshly ground black pepper to taste
st: Whisk together thegarlic, cumin, cardamom, lime juice, lime zest, salt, pepper and 2 teaspoons of the olive oil and transfer to a sealable plastic bag just large enough to hold the lamb chops.
Add the lamb chops, seal the bag, forcing out the excess air, and massage the lamb until it is coated.
Marinate at room tempreture for about 15 minutes, turning the bag occasionally.
Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large non-stick pan over a high heat until hot but not smoking.
Cook half of the chops for about 3-5 minutes on each side, transfer them to a platter and cover with foil.
Wipe out the pan, then heat the remaining olive oil and cook the remaining chops in the same way.
Transfer the chops to a warmed platter and serve with fresh coriander, pomegranate rubies and lime halves.

ing: 1 kg whole beef fillet, sinews and fat removed
st: Bring the beef fillet to room temperature and season well and rub with the canola oil.
Warm a pan to very hot and brown the beef fillet on all sides.
Place the fillet on a rack in a roasting tray. Bruise the herbs and place the sprigs on top of the fillet. Cover with foil and bring to room temperature before placing in the oven.
Remove the foil, and place the fillet in a preheated 230Â°C hot oven for 5 minutes then turn the heat down to 200Â°C and continue cooking for another 5-10 minutes.
Check the doneness of the meat â it should best be served medium, cooking times will depend on the thickness of the fillet.
Allow the meat to rest for at least 15 minutes then carve into medallions and serve dressed with salsa verde.

t: Lemon tart with coconut and date crust
st: Pre-heat oven to 170ËC.
Place coconut, dates and water in a food processer and blend until smooth.
Press coconut mixture into a greased 30cm tart case.
Bake tart cases in the oven for 15 minutes or until dry.
Place butter, sugar and lemon juice in a bowl over a double boiler.
Whisk the mixture until the sugar has dissolved.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, whisk them up and slowly add to the lemon mixture.
Whisk until the lemon mixture thickens, the mixture needs to be able to coat the back of a spoon.
Pour into tart case and place in the refrigerator to set.
Store any extra lemon curd in a sterilized jars. Lemon curd will last in the fridge for a few weeks.

ing: 250 ml mixed nuts, chopped, raw and unsalted
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.
Combine all the ingredients except the dried apricots and oats in a bowl and mix well.
Allow the mixture to stand for 10 minutes, then add the oats, mix well again and spread out over a baking sheet.
Roast the mixture for about 20 minutes, stirring it often, until it is golden.
Remove from the oven, allow to cool and add the dried apricots.
Store in an airtight container or jar.

ing: 300 g brown lentils (or use tinned lentils, drained and rinsed)
st: Soak the lentils in 1.5l of water overnight.

Bring a large pot of water to the boil and add the drained lentils. When lentils are al dente add a large pinch of salt and continue to cook for another ten minutes, then remove from the stove and strain through a fine colander or sieve.  Run under cold water to cool the lentils down.
Allow the lentils to drain in the colander. An alternative is to use tinned lentils, drained and rinsed.
Preheat the oven to 200ËC. Peel the pumpkin and cut into 2cm thick wedges. Place the wedges on a tray, brush with olive oil, lightly season and roast for about 35 minutes until golden and soft.
Chop the red onion, chili and parsley very fine and add to the drained lentils with 15ml olive oil. Add the lemon zest and lemon juice.  Lastly season with salt and pepper.
Place washed wild rocket evenly around the platter and arrange pumpkin on top of the lentil salad. Crumble the feta cheese over the top.

ing: 2 tins haricot beans, drained and rinsed
1 kg lamb leg cubes, trimmed of fat
st: Finely chop onions, carrots and celery making sure to keep them separated.
Warm a large pot, add the oil and brown the lamb cubes.  Cook the lamb until evenly browned all over.  Remove from the pot and set aside.
Add the onions to the pot and sautÃ© until they are opaque, then add the carrots and cook for 5 minutes then add the celery and cook for another 5 minutes.
Return the lamb to the pot with the tomato paste. Cook for 5 minutes then use a bit of stock to deglaze the bottom of the pot, scraping of any caramelized bits.
Add the beef stock and rosemary. Bring to the boil then lower the heat and simmer for one and a half hours stirring occasionally.
Peel the rainbow carrots and set aside until needed.
Open the tins of haricot beans, strain and rinse them.  Set aside until needed.
When the lamb has been cooing for an hour and a half add the carrots and after 20 minutes the haricot beans.
Check the seasoning before serving.
Serve with pearled barley or brown rice, garnished with more rosemary.

ing: 10 g freshly grated Grana Padano / Parmesan to serve
500 g fresh ripe plum tomatoes, skinned and chopped
150 g carrots, peeled and cut into even blocks
150 g baby marrows, cut into even blocks
150 g Celery, cut into even blocks
st: SautÃ© the onions, celery, carrots, cabbage and garlic until the onions are translucent.
Add the stock, quinoa and tomatoes and cook for about 25 minutes. (Check that the carrots are almost soft)
Add the courgettes and beans and simmer for another 20 minutes.
Check the seasoning.
Just before serving stir in the basil leaves. Add black pepper and finish with grated parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

t: Herb salad with poached egg & parmesan
st: To make the dressing, combine the oil, zest and lemon juice. Season with a pinch of salt and set aside.
Trim the stalks of the herbs, reserving only the leaves. Larger leaves can be torn into smaller pieces. Wash and dry the leaves very well in a salad spinner.
Poach the eggs and keep them warm.
To plate individual salads for a starter, lightly dress the herbs with the dressing and divide between four plates.
Divide the parmesan shavings between the plates and place them between the leaves.
Make a ânestâ between the herbs and place the poached egg in the centre.
Drizzle with a last bit of dressing and top the egg with cracked black pepper and Maldon salt.
Serve with the egg still warm.

ing: 1 kg baby bok choy, washed and halved lengthways
60 g lemon grass trimmed and finely chopped
15 g fresh ginger, peeled and grated
st: Heat the canola oil in a large wok, add the garlic, ginger, lemon grass, chilies, soy sauce and sugar and stir fry for 1-2 minutes.
Add the bock choy and spring onion and 1tbsp of water and stir fry for 1 minute until the leaves are wilted.
Sprinkle with the rice vinegar, stir once and serve in a big platter.

ing: 100 g kalamata olives, pitted and chopped
1/2 cup Sun-dried tomatoes, chopped plus extra for serving
st: Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy skillet over a medium-high heat and add the onion, garlic, rosemary and oregano.
SautÃ© for about 5 minutes until the onion is tender, then add the tomatoes with the juices, artichokes, sun-dried tomatoes and olives.
Simmer for about 3 minutes until the sauce has thickened slightly. Season to taste with black pepper.
Cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling, salted water until just tender but still firm to the bite.
Drain the pasta, reserving 1 cup of the cooking liquid.
Return the pasta to the same pot, add the sauce and toss over a medium heat until the sauce coats the pasta. Add the reserved cooking liquid by 1/4 cupfuls if the pasta is too dry.
Add half of the feta, 1/2 cup of the basil and toss to combine.
To serve, transfer the pasta to a serving bowl and sprinkle with the remaining feta and basil.

ing: 1 large lime, sliced in thin slices and quartered
st: Place water in the fridge and allow to chill.  To speed up the process place water in the freezer.
Place the lime slices in the jug.  Muddle the lime a bit so that the juices and flavours can be released.
Add the lavender petals and ice then fill up with the chilled water.
Return to the fridge or serve immediately.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 x 80 g packet Woolworths hand-shelled fresh peas
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Heat the olive oil and butter in an ovenproof pan and fry the leeks until soft and golden. Add the peas.
Beat the eggs, cream and Parmesan. Pour over the leeks and peas and add the spaghetti. Cook over a medium heat for 5 minutes.
Place the pan in the oven and bake for 15â20 minutes, or until the egg has set.
Turn out onto a plate, cut into wedges and season to taste before serving.

ing: 4 cups cake flour, plus more for dusting
st: For the naan breads, sift the flour, salt and baking powder in a large bowl and set aside.
Mix together the water, yeast and sugar and whisk together until they are completely dissolved, then allow the mixture to rest for 10 minutes.
Add in the warm milk, sour cream, yoghurt and oil and mix together until combined.
Pour the yeast mixture into the bowl of dry ingredients and mix together until completely combined and starts to form a sticky dough.
Transfer the dough onto a heavily floured surface and knead for 3 â 4 minutes until smooth.
Once smooth, form the dough into a ball, place in a lightly greased large bowl, cover with a damp cloth and allow to rise for 1 â 1Â½1/2 hours.
Once the dough has risen, knock it back, and form it into 8 equal sized dough balls.
Transfer the dough balls back to the floured work surface and use a rolling pin to roll each ball into an oval about 15 â 17 cm long.
Heat a cast iron skillet over a medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, brush one side of the dough with melted butter and place it butter side down on the skillet.
Cook for 1 â 2 minutes then flip and cook for an additional 1 â 2 minutes. Repeat until all the naan breads have been cooked.
To make the flavoured butter, mix together the butter, curry powder and olive oil, then add the coriander, garlic and salt and mix until combined.
Serve the flavoured butter and warm naan breads with crunchy radishes.

ing: 2 tbsp mixed with 2 tbsp cold water corn flour
4 cloves garlic, peeled and roughly chopped
salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Preheat the oven to 200 Â°C.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy-based saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 4 â 5 minutes or until softened.
Add the garlic and curry paste and cook for another 2 minutes.
Add the dates, soya sauce, chicken stock and corn flour mixture to the pan and mix well.
Bring to a boil then reduce to a simmer, cover and leave to cook for 30 minutes. Allow to cool slightly.
Blend until smooth then pass through a sieve, discarding any solids.
Add the lime juice and season to taste.
Put the chicken breasts, one at a time, between sheets of clingfilm and beat with a rolling pin until flattened by half.
Dust the chicken pieces with the flour, dip them in the beaten egg, then cover them in the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a large heavy-based frying pan, and brown the chicken on each side.
Place the chicken on a foil-lined baking tray for 8 â 10 minutes or until cooked through.
Serve the crispy chicken breasts with the curry sauce and sticky rice.

ing: 1 x 5  cm ginger piece, peeled and finely chopped
1 spring onion, thinly sliced, to garnish
1 x 75  g Woolworths Asian Chinese prawn crackers bag
4 free-range chicken breasts, cut into large chunks
st: Place all the ingredients in the wok and cook, stirring, until the sugar has just dissolved.
Return the chicken to the wok and toss to coat in the glaze. Cook until the chicken is cooked through. Serve immediately with the prawn crackers and beetroot onion pickle. Garnish with spring onion.

ing: 1 cup Woolworths Spicy Korean BBQ Marinade
2 tbsp Woolworths Mama Oâs Premium Super Spicy Pepper Paste
2 tbsp Woolworths Mama O's Premium Super Spicy Pepper Paste
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.

Place the chicken stock, garlic, carrot, celery and oxtail into a large ovenproof dish with a tight-fitting lid. Cook in the oven for 2 hours, or until the meat is tender and almost falling off the bone.
Remove the oxtail from the dish and set aside. The cooking liquid can be strained and frozen for a tasty beef stock.
Pour some of the Asian-style glaze into a pan, add the oxtail in batches and cook until the meat is coated in the marinade and sticky.
Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat.
Cut the brinjals into small cubes. Fry the brinjals in batches, then drain on kitchen paper.
Return the brinjals to the pan and add the soya sauce, fish sauce, sugar and vinegar.
Grate the ginger, garlic and chop the chilli finely.
Scatter with the chopped spring onions.
Serve tossed into noodles or as a side dish for an Asian-grilled chicken breast.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
2 kg free range leg of lamb
a handful fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.
Rub the lamb with 2 T olive oil, salt and pepper. Roast for 20 minutes.
Remove from the oven and smear the harissa all over the lamb using the back of a spoon, then return to the oven and reduce the temperature to 160Â°C and roast for a further 60â70 minutes.

Toss the beetroot in 1 T olive oil and season to taste, then carefully add to the same dish as the lamb for the last 40 minutes of cooking time. If the outer layer of the lamb starts to catch, cover it in foil.

Remove the lamb from the oven, cover with foil and leave to rest for 15 minutes before carving. Add the remaining olive oil to the cooked couscous, toss with the mint and Â¾ cup pomegranate rubies, and season to taste.
Serve the couscous with the lamb and beetroot and sprinkle over the remaining pomegranate rubies. Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve the yoghurt on the side.

t: Honey and mascarpone pecan nut buns
ing: 5-6 cups flour, plus more for kneading
200 ml honey, plus more for brushing and drizzling
1 cup full cream milk, room temperature
st: Whisk the milk, 230 g of butter, 80 ml of honey, salt, vanilla and the eggs in a mixer on a medium speed.
Add the yeast and 1/3 cup of lukewarm water, and whisk for 1 minute.
Change to a dough hook, reduce the speed to low, and add 4 cups of flour. After the flour is incorporated, raise the speed to medium, and continue kneading.
Add the remaining flour, one cup at a time, mixing until the dough no longer sticks to the bowl. Raise the speed to medium-high and knead for 10 minutes.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes by hand on a floured surface until smooth.
Transfer to an oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour until it has doubled in size.
For the topping, melt the remaining butter in a saucepan over a medium heat.
Stir in 120 ml of honey, the syrup and white sugar, and bring to a gentle simmer. Remove from the heat and allow to cool.
For the filling, combine the mascarpone and crÃ¨me fraÃ®che in a bowl.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface, divide into 3 and shape into 3 balls.
Roll the balls of dough into 25 cm by 36 cm rectangles and brush lightly with honey.
Spread the mascarpone mixture evenly on top of the rectangles, leaving a 2.5 cm border all around. Sprinkle with the pecan nuts.
Starting on one long side, roll the dough into a log. Pinch along the seam to seal, then cut into nine 4 cm-thick slices.
Pour the honey mixture into a 20 cm square baking pan. Place the buns, cut-side down, in the pan, 3 or 4 to a row.
Let the buns rise in a warm, draft-free area for about 40 minutes until doubled in size.
Preheat the oven to 190 Â°C and place the oven rack in the lower third of the oven.
Bake the buns for about 45 minutes to 1 hour, rotating halfway through, until brown and bubbling. If the buns start to darken too quickly, cover them with foil.
Once baked, immediately invert the buns onto a wire rack on a baking tray, drizzle them with honey and serve warm.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 purple spring onions, thinly sliced at an angle
2 red peppers, deseeded and cut into halves and quarters
3 baby brinjals, sliced lengthwise or halved
1 tbsp spicy harissa red pepper paste
st: For the dressing, mix together 3 tablespoons of the olive oil, honey and harissa paste. Set aside.
Tip the bulgur wheat into a large bowl and pour over enough boiling water to cover. Let it stand for 10 minutes until tender and plump.
Heat a griddle pan over a medium heat.

Brush the sliced vegetables with olive oil and grill in a single layer, turning occasionally, for about 10 â 15 minutes, until lightly charred and tender. During the last 5 minutes of cooking, baste the brinjals with the honey harissa dressing.
Drizzle half of the remaining dressing over the warm brinjals and peppers. Season well.
Drain the bulgur wheat and pour over the remaining dressing. Add the lemon juice, lemon zest, spring onion, coriander and mint leaves. Season well and toss together.
Serve the bulgur wheat on a platter, topped with grilled vegetables and dotted with double cream yoghurt if desired.
Combine the 3 cups of flour, eggs, butter, salt and baking powder in a large mixing bowl. Mix well for 3 to 4 minutes until a soft dough forms.
Divide the dough into four equal parts and shape into balls.
On a floured work surface, roll the dough balls into long, 5 cm-thick ropes.
Cut the ropes into 2.5 cm pieces, dust with flour and place onto a floured baking sheet.
Heat a small non-stick pan over a medium heat and toast the flaked almonds for about 2 minutes, stirring frequently, until just golden brown. Remove from the heat and set aside.
In a large sautÃ© pan over a medium-high heat, combine the honey, orange zest and a cup of water. Bring to a boil, then immediately reduce to a simmer.
Heat the canola oil to 190 Â°C in a large pot.
In batches, fry the doughnuts in the hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes until golden brown and puffed on all sides.
Remove them with a slotted spoon and toss in the orange syrup to coat.
Transfer to a plate and sprinkle with the toasted flaked almonds. Serve immediately.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
8 chicken thighs, skinless, deboned and cubed
1/4 cup fresh lime juice, plus wedges for serving
2 tsp fresh ginger, peeled and finely chopped
st: Preheat the oven to 190 Â°C.
Whisk the garlic, ginger, lime juice, soy sauce and honey in a large bowl. Add the chicken and toss to coat. Let the chicken marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread the chicken cubes onto 4 skewers.
Place the chicken and marinade on a foil-lined rimmed baking tray and roast for about 15 â 20 minutes until cooked through and sticky.
While cooking the chicken, toss the asparagus and spring onions with sunflower oil and place on another rimmed baking sheet.
Season with salt and pepper and roast for 10 â 15 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until tender.
Remove the chicken from the skewers and serve warm with the roasted asparagus and spring onion, topped with fresh coriander.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
1  big handful Italian parsley, finely chopped
st: Slice the thighs 2 â 3 times at intervals without cutting through the chicken completely.
Mix the mustard, olive oil and honey together and season well with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Coat the chicken in the honey marinade and leave for 30 minutes or covered in the fridge overnight.
Preheat the oven to 200 Â°C.
Put the chicken, skin-side up, on a foil-lined baking tray. Bake for about 20 â 30 minutes until cooked and browned.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a pan and add the leeks. Squeeze over the lemon juice and sprinkle with the sugar.
Bring to a boil, cover and leave on a low simmer for 20 â 30 minutes or until the leeks have softened.
Toss the breadcrumbs and garlic in olive oil and toast in the oven for 5 minutes.
To serve, top the braised leeks with the chicken thighs, spoon over any cooking juices and scatter with the garlic crumbs and Italian parsley.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Mix the pomegranate concentrate and honey and pour the marinade over the pork. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper and leave for a few hours or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 200 Â°C.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a frying pan and sear the pork fillets on all sides.
Place the fillets in a roasting tin lined with foil, together with the remaining marinade and onion wedges. Drizzle with the remaining vegetable oil and roast for 30 minutes.
Slice the pork fillets.

To serve, place the onion wedges on a serving dish, drizzled with the lemon juice, together with the rocket, parsley and sumac and topped with the pork fillets. Add the pan juices and scatter with the pomegranate rubies.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Preheat to oven to 160 Â°C.
Combine the olive oil, vinegar, thyme, salt and pepper and brush over the lamb and brinjal slices.
Place the lamb, uncovered with the fat-side up, on the rack of a roasting pan.
Roast for 20 minutes plus 15 â 25 minutes per 500 g until done to your liking. Allow to rest for 10 minutes before carving.
Cook the brinjals on a hot grill pan for 3 â 4 minutes on each side or until golden and tender.
Combine the lemon juice and honey.
Slice the lamb into 2 or 3 cutlets per person.
Serve the lamb cutlets with the grilled brinjals, mint, dill and feta, drizzled with the lemon and honey mixture.
Boil the potato in its jacket. Then, while still hot, peel and mash until smooth.
Sift the flour, 50g of the sugar, and salt. Stir in the spices and naartjie peel.
Rub in 4 T of oil and the potato to form a crumbly mixture.
Mix the milk and water, then add the yeast and 1 t sugar, then mix to dissolve.
Add the milk mixture and egg to the dry ingredients and mix well to form a very soft and sticky dough.
Moisten your hands with a little oil and rub them over the dough, cover and set aside for two hours, or until doubled in size.
Generously coat your hands in oil and knock down the dough.
Place on a well-oiled surface and divide into 12-16 balls. Again, allow the dough to double in size (30-40 minutes)
Heat the remaining oil in a large saucepan and, when hot, fry the koesisters until golden. Drain on kitchen paper.
Place the koesisters in the syrup and place over a low heat to soak for at least 20 minutes.
Remove from the syrup and roll in the coconut mixture. Serve warm.
To make the syrup, dissolve the sugar in the water over a low heat. Once dissolved, bring the syrup to a boil and cook for 5 minutes.
To make the coconut coating, place the coconut, dried naartjie peel and cinnamon in a pan and toast until golden brown. Allow to cool, then add the fresh naartjie zest.

ing: 1 x 500 g packet Woolworths tagliatelle pasta, cooked al dente, for serving
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 x 800 g Woolworths Italian whole peeled tomatoes can, blended
200 g leeks, washed and roughly chopped
freshly ground black pepper to taste
st: To make the tomato sauce, heat the olive oil and butter in a pan over a medium heat. Add the leeks and onions and cook until soft, seasoning with salt. Add the garlic, rosemary and thyme and cook for 3 minutes, then pour in the wine.
Reduce the wine by half, then add the beef stock, balsamic vinegar, tomatoes and tomato paste. Season with pepper. Cook, covered, over a low heat for 45 minutes.
To make the meatballs, preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Soak the bread in the milk. Squeeze out any excess milk and place in a large bowl. Add the mince, onion, parsley and Parmesan and season to taste.
Mix using your hands. Roll into 20 small balls or 15 slightly larger ones.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over a medium heat. Brown the meatballs in batches, taking care not to overcrowd the pan.
Arrange the meatballs on a baking tray and finish in the oven for about 10 minutes.
Place the pasta in a serving dish. Mix the meatballs and tomato sauce, then spoon over the pasta. Serve with Parmesan and garnish with basil.

ing: 1 x 350 g punnet Woolworths exotic tomatoes, halved
2 tbsp Maldon smoked sea salt flakes
st: To make the ricotta, place the milk, cream and salt into a large saucepan. Heat the mixture over a medium heat for 5 minutes, or until it reaches 82Â°C â use a thermometer to check the temperature. Make sure the mixture does not boil.
Remove from the heat, then gradually add the vinegar while stirring. Allow to stand while the milk solids coagulate and float to the surface.
Spoon the solids into a sieve, reserving the whey. Place the solids into a clean piece of cheesecloth and squeeze out as much liquid as possible, reserving the whey.
Place the ricotta in a sieve over a bowl and drain for 1 hour, then chill.
To make the exotic tomato salad, whisk the olive oil, apple cider vinegar, chilli flakes and salt and mix through tomatoes. Serve with the ricotta.

t: Herbed tomato mince with cheesy polenta
ing: 1 x 800 g can Italian whole peeled tomatoes, crushed
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Soften the onion, celery and carrot in the oil, then stir in the garlic.
Add the mince and stir until browned. Add the tomatoes, stock, herbs, celery leaves and seasoning. Cover and simmer for 50 minutes.
Stir in the balsamic vinegar. Cook uncovered over a brisk heat for 5â10 minutes to reduce the liquid if necessary. Check the seasoning.
To make the cheesy polenta, cook the polenta according to package instructions, then whisk in enough boiling water to create a loose consistency. Stir in the cheese and season. Serve with the mince.

ing: 100 g good quality dark chocolate, melted
100 g Woolworths rose flavoured turkish delight
100 g pistachios, lightly toasted and chopped
1 L Woolworths free from lactose vanilla ice cream
st: Remove the ice cream 20 â 30 minutes before you begin making the dessert. Add the slightly melted ice cream to a food mixer or to a large bowl.
Add the pistachios and Turkish delight before mixing through and returning to a serving dish that is freezer safe.

Place the dish in the freezer to allow the ice cream to freeze. Once set remove from the freezer and drizzle over the melted chocolate and serve. If youâre not going to finish it all simply cover with a lid that is air tight before returning to the freezer.

ing: 1 cup Woolworths free from lactose low fat plain yoghurt
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
50 g Woolworths Indian Tikka Masala Paste
500 g Woolworths Free from Lactose Low Fat Plain Yoghurt
st: In a large mixing bowl combine the 500 g yoghurt, 50 g tikka masala, 4 tbsp roughly chopped coriander, 4 tbsp roughly chopped mint and salt and pepper for seasoning. Add the 8 chicken thighs and massage for a minute before allowing to marinade for 15 â 30 minute or overnight if you have the time.

While the chicken is marinating prepare the raita: Combine all the ingredients (1/2 grated English cucmber, 4 tbsp desiccated coconut, 4 tbsp roughly chopped mint, 1 cup Woolworths free from lactose low fat plain yoghurt, salt to taste) together and allow to sit.

Heat a griddle pan over a high heat. Add the chicken thighs and grill for about 4 minutes a side. Turn over and cook the other side in the same way. Finish with a squeeze of lime or lemon and serve with the raita and naan or rice.

ing: fresh blueberries and toasted almonds to serve
1 Free from gluten white bread loaf
st: Slice the bread into 8 medium-thick slices.
In a bowl, lightly crush the blueberries then mix in the mascarpone cheese, honey and orange zest.
Place a generous mound of mascarpone onto 4 of the bread slices, then top with another slice.
Whisk together the eggs, cream, salt, cinnamon and more honey to taste.
Dip the sandwiches into the egg to coat well.
Melt the butter and oil in a pan, then gently fry the French toast in the pan until golden brown on each side.
Serve warm, drizzled with more honey if desired, sprinkled with blueberries and toasted almonds.

ing: a small bunch mint leaves, picked and roughly chopped
a small bunch fresh mint leaves, picked and roughly chopped
st: In a large bowl, mix all the kofta ingredients, apart from the olive oil, with your hands until well combined. Test the seasoning by frying a small ball of the mince mixture and tasting it once cooked through.
Shape the mince mixture into small, slightly flattened sausage shapes, about half the size of your palm. Cover and chill for 30 minutes.
To make the tzatziki, mix 1 teaspoon of salt with the grated cucumber and leave it in a sieve with a bowl underneath to collect the moisture.
In a small bowl, mix the remaining ingredients, apart from the extra virgin olive oil.
Squeeze as much liquid out of the cucumber as possible to avoid a watery tzatziki, then stir the cucumber through the yoghurt mixture.
To braai the koftas, thread the sausages carefully onto skewers and grill until cooked through.
Alternatively, preheat the oven to 180Â°C.

Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan and fry the kofta sausages in batches for about 2 minutes on each side until browned. Transfer them to a baking tray and cook them in the and cook them in the coven for about 10 minutes until cooked through.
Drizzle the tzatziki with the extra virgin olive oil and serve with the hot koftas.

ing: extra virgin olive oil, for drizzling
Woolworths multiseed wraps, cut into large triangles and lightly toasted
1 cup Woolworths sweet sticky BBQ marinade
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat oven to 180Â°C. Coat the ribbetjies in the seasoning before placing on a roasting tray and roasting in the oven for 15 minutes. Reduce the heat to 160Â°C and add the carrots that have been coated in the olive oil and seasoning. Allow them to roast with the lamb for 30 â 40 minutes.
Baste the meat with the BBQ marinade every 10 minutes until they become sweet and sticky. Remove the dish from the oven and add the lamb to a serving platter.
Squeeze the fresh lemon over the carrots before adding to the serving platter. Garnish with the parsley and serve with the hummus and flatbread.
To prepare the hummus: Add the hummus to a serving bowl before scattering over the spring onions, lemon zest and extra virgin olive oil.

t: Light and fresh grilled chicken burger
ing: 4 cups Woolworths fat free Ayrshire yoghurt
550 g Woolworths bulk papaya and citrus fruit salad
450 g Woolworths herb salad, vegetables separated
extra virgin olive oil, to brush
st: To get the perfect cross hatch on a burger. Heat the griddle pan over a high heat. Brush the chicken patty with the olive oil before placing on the griddle pan.

Allow the patty to cook for 2-3 minutes before checking if char lines have formed, if so carefully slice a spatula under the burger and turn it 90Â°C. Allow to cook for another 2-3 minutes before turning over a cooking the other side in the same manner.
Slice through the buns before coating lightly with the mayonnaise. Add it to the griddle pan to toast for a few minutes.
Add the lettuce from the salad selection to the base of the buns before layering the remaining vegetables. Top with the chicken patty and finish off with the tops of the buns.
Serve with bulk papaya and citrus fruit salad on plain yoghurt with a drizzle of honey.

ing: 4 Woolworths pita bread, toasted, to serve
1 baby cucumber, cut into ribbons using a vegetable peeler (discard the seeds)
1 carrot, cut into ribbons using a vegetable peeler
st: In a large bowl, mix together the lamb mince, cream cheese, cumin, ground coriander, fresh coriander, mint, lemon zest, lemon juice, pine nuts and seasoning.

Divide the mixture into 8 equal balls, then squash each ball onto the skewer with your hand to form a sausage around the skewer â the mixture should be knubbly and have indents from your fingers in it.
Place the koftas onto a hot braai, then sear on all sides until cooked through.
For the pickle, place the water, vinegar, sugar and fennel into a pot, then bring to a simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat.
Place the vegetables into a bowl, then pour the liquid onto the vegetables and leave to sit for 30 minutes.

To serve, toast the pita breads, then cut in half. Fill with some tzatziki and pickled vegetables, then top with a kofta (removed from the skewer). Drizzle with a little extra tzatziki over the kofta to serve.

ing: 255 g easy to cook vegetable spaghetti
salt and freshly ground black pepper
125 g Woolworths roasted red pepper pesto
235 g Easy to cook baby marrow and spinach
st: In a large oven proof dish add the rainbow carrots, then layer in the remaining vegetables.
Mix together the red pepper pesto, garlic, seasoning and cream.
Pour over the layered vegetables.
Combine pesto, parmesan and breadcrumbs.
Sprinkle over the vegetables.
Bake at 180 for 35 â 40 minutes, until golden.
Serve.

ing: 200 g Woolworths ready to eat poached lemon & pepper trout
st: Preheat oven to 200Â°C.
Grease a 12-hole muffin pan.
Cut the courgettes into thin strips using a vegetable peeler then line the muffin pan with the courgette ribbons.
Flake the trout into big pieces, then place into the muffin cups.
Whisk together the eggs, seasoning, sour cream and Parmesan cheese.
Pour into the cups then place into the oven and bake until the egg are puffed and cooked through.
Serve on toasted sourdough bread.

Place the chicken, vegetables (2 roughly chopped carrots, 1 roughly chopped onion), herbs (4 sprigs of thyme, a handful of parsley stalks and 2 bay leaves), 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper into a large pot, then cover with cold water.
Bring to the boil, then turn down to a simmer.
Cover the pot then leave chicken to poach for 30 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the stock, then set aside to cool, reserving the stock.

While the chicken cools, make the pastry: Place 225 g cake flour and 1/2 tsp salt into a bowl, then rub in the 125 g cold, chopped butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs then mix in the 1/2 cup of grated parmesan. Add the 3 egg yolks, then mix together to form a dough â if the mixture is too dry, add a little cold water until the pastry comes together into a ball.
Wrap pastry in cling film and leave to rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Melt the 1/4 cup butter in a large saucepan, then stir in the 1/4 cup flour and cook for 2 minutes over low heat.
Whisk in 3 cups of the strained, reserved stock, then add the 250 ml milk.
Leave to simmer for 10 minutes.
Shred the chicken into large chunks, discarding any bones and skin then stir into the sauce along with the 2 tbsp chopped parsley, season with salt and pepper to taste.
Heat a pan and melt 2 tbsp butter, add the 200 g sliced mushrooms, then saute until golden on the edges and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir mushrooms into the chicken mixture then transfer mixture to a pie dish. Season to taste.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Roll pastry out then cut a few holes into the pastry before placing onto the filling.
Brush with egg wash, then bake for 30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and crisp.
Serve hot with a Crunchy Salad on the side.
