ing: Pears peeled, and poached in verjuice, honey and star anise
Daikon ribbons, made with a vegetable peeler
cucumber ribbons and coconut ribbons, made with a vegetable peeler
st: Slice the cheese horizontally to make three layers. Layer with the ribbons, and garnish with the pears.
Serve with crackers or biscotti.

Bring the cream and sugar to a slow boil and cook for 3â4 minutes. Remove from the heat, whisking to dissolve the sugar. Add the lemon juice and zest, it should be quite tart and sharp. Allow to cool to room temperature, then pour into glasses and chill for 4 hours or overnight. It should be only just set and silky in texture.

To make the red-wine snow, bring the wine, sugar and cinnamon to a boil and cook for 5 minutes. Remove from heat and allow to cool for 20 minutes. Remove the cinnamon stick, pour into a tray and place into the freezer. After about 4 hours, it should be set. Flake with a fork to make snow just before serving.

t: Load shedding rice with smoked trout
ing: 1 x 10 cm ginger piece, peeled and roughly chopped
st: Pound the lemongrass and ginger into a coarse paste using a pestle and mortar. Transfer to a saucepan and add the rice, salt, chicken stock and water. Cook according to package instructions.
Place the trout, skin side down, in a pan over a high heat and cook until the skin is golden and crisp.

Serve with the rice and drizzle over the soya sauce. Place the sliced spring onion in iced water for a few minutes until it curls. Garnish with the spring onion, chilli, basil leaves and squeeze over the limes.

ing: 1 Woolworths Free Range Rosemary, Lemon & Garlic Partly Deboned Leg Of Lamb
st: Cook the lamb as per the package instructions.
Preheat oven to 200C
To make the potatoes, peel then cut into chunks and place into a pot of cold water. Season with salt, then boil until potatoes are just tender â do not over-boil the potatoes at this stage.
Drain potatoes and set aside to air dry on a tray lined with kitchen paper.
Place the duck fat, sage and thyme into a roasting dish, then place into the oven to heat for 15 minutes.
Once the fat is hot and melted, place the potatoes into the roasting dish, season generously with salt, then toss to cover the potatoes in the fat.
Return to the oven, then roast potatoes for 30 minutes or until golden and crisp.
For the carrots, cut them into thick diagonal slices, then place into a pot with the water, cover with a lid, then simmer until the carrots are tender.
Remove the lid then add the butter and the honey â increase the heat and saute the carrots until sticky and glazed. Toss in the parsley, then serve immediately.
For the mint sauce, pour the water onto the sugar, then stir to dissolve.
Add the vinegar, mint and salt, then leave to stand for 20 minutes before serving spooned onto the lamb.

ing: 4 ripe mangoes, diced, plus extra for serving (optional)
st: PurÃ©e half the mango and pour into a saucepan along with the remaining ingredients. Place over a medium heat and stir until the mixture thickens.
Remove from the heat and chill. PurÃ©e the remaining mango and add to the chilled mixture.
Spoon into an ice-cream machine and churn according to the manufacturerâs instructions.
Serve frozen with extra fresh mango on the side, if using.

ing: 3 x 40 g seed crackers & peanut butter dip
2 x 5 g roasted seaweed snack wasabi
st: Preheat oven to 180C.
Place the oven onto a tray, then roast for 10 minutes or until roasted and golden.
Remove from the oven, then drizzle with olive oil.
Crush the seaweed snack, then scatter over the nuts along with the sesame seeds and toss well.
Leave to cool completely before storing in an airtight container

ing: 1 x 2 cm ginger piece, finely grated
st: Slice a large wedge out of the watermelon and peel.
Using a vegetable peeler, shave thin ribbons from the cucumber and green mango and place in a large mixing bowl. Add the baby herb leaves and mint and toss through.
Pile the salad on the wedge of watermelon. Drizzle over the dressing and chilli yoghurt

ing: 2 cauliflower, small head, cut into florets
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Heat the olive oil over a medium heat before adding the onion and garlic. Cook slowly allowing the onions to soften and slightly caramelise.
Add the cauliflower florets along with a little water, just enough to create some steam. Slowly simmer with the lid on until the cauliflower becomes tender, and breaks apart easily.
Add the parmesan to the cooked cauliflower and blend together until smooth using a hand blender. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Stir the sauce through the cooked pasta and top with the crisp Parmesan sprinkle.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 large butternut, skinned and cut into thin discs
2 sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into thin discs
3 beetroot, peeled and cut into thin discs
salt and freshly ground black pepper
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Add the leeks, thyme, garlic and cream in a pan. Simmer over a medium heat as the cream reduces. Once the cream has reduced by half season with salt and freshly ground black pepper before taking off the heat.
Grease a large spring form tin before adding the ribbons of marrow along the outside of the tin, creating a border.
Begin layering the vegetables adding some of the filling and spreading it roughly with every few layers.

Continue creating a border with the marrow and layering vegetables with the filling. Cover the top with foil before placing the tin in the oven to cook for 1 hour at 180Â°C or until the vegetables are cooked and tender.

Remove the foil and cook for another 15 minutes at 220Â°C to caramelize and brown. Take the dish out the oven and allow it to cool slightly before removing from the tin and placing it on a serving dish and allow it to reach room temperature.
Spread the topping over the vegetable cake as you would ice a cake. Arrange the micro vegetables on the cake as a topping. Slice and serve.

Heat the oil over a medium heat. Add the lamb to the pot and brown evenly before setting aside. To the same pot add the onions and cook until tender then add the garlic and ginger before cooking it for another 1 minute.
Add the spices, curry leaves and chilli then cook until fragrant. Add the tomatoes and coconut milk before returning the lamb to the pot. Season with salt to taste
Simmer gently for 45 minutes with the lid on over a low heat. If the meat needs to be more tender cook the dish for another 20 minutes.
Serve the curry with the cooked basmati rice and garnish with the coriander

t: Lamb meatballs in warm yoghurt sauce
ing: 2 tbsp fresh dill, chopped plus extra for garnish
1/2 tsp cumin seeds, toasted and ground
st: Heat a large pan over a medium heat. Add the olive oil and swirl to coat. When the oil is hot, add the meatballs; they should fit in a single layer. Fry gently, turning the meatballs with two soup spoons so they brown on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Using a slotted spoon, transfer the meatballs to a plate. Pour off and discard any fat in the pan.
Return the pan to a medium-high heat and add the stock. Stir with a wooden spoon to scrape up any browned bits on the bottom of the pan and simmer for a few minutes.
Return the meatballs to the pan, cover, and reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, and then transfer the meatballs to a plate using a slotted spoon.

In a large bowl, whisk together the yoghurt, egg, garlic, dill and mint. Slowly whisk in about Â½ cup of the hot stock to warm the yoghurt and then pour the yoghurt mixture into the pan. Cook over a medium-low heat, stirring with a wooden spoon, until the sauce visibly thickens and just begins to simmer. Add salt and pepper to taste. Return the meatballs to the pan and turn to coat them with the sauce. Cover and simmer gently until hot.
Divide the meatballs and sauce among 4 warmed bowls.
Put the butter in a small saucepan set over a medium heat. When the butter melts, add the paprika and cumin and swirl the pan until the butter foams and sizzles and you can smell the spices.
Drizzle each portion with some of the red-pepper butter. Garnish with chopped dill.

t: How to make marbled easter eggs
st: Divide the water and vinegar between two medium-sized bowls.

Add 10 to 20 drops of green food colouring to one bowl, and the same amount of blue food colouring to the other. The amount of food colouring you add will determine the depth of colour. Stir both mixtures to combine.
One at a time, submerge the eggs into the bowl of green dye for a few minutes.
Remove the eggs from the dye and place on a sheet of kitchen paper to allow the colour to dry and deepen.
Add the olive oil to the bowl of blue food colouring and stir. The mixture should be no deeper than 5 cm and the dye should be a deeper or contrasting hue to the green food colouring.
Hold the egg between the thumb and finger of one hand and use the other hand to rotate it in the dye, allowing the oil to create the desired marbling effect.
Remove the egg from the dye and pat dry. Repeat with the remaining eggs.

Preheat oven to 180C
Cut the hot cross buns into cubes then place into a greased oven dish, along with the white chocolate chips.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, pumpkin, castor sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, cream and salt, then pour onto the hot cross buns and leave to stand for 10 minutes.
Mix together the sugar and cinnamon, then sprinkle over the pudding.
Dot with the butter, then bake for 45 minutes in a bain marie until the custard has set.
Serve with vanilla ice cream.

ing: 1 pack chocolate chip hot cross buns
st: Arrange the hot cross buns in the waffle iron ensuring they overlap slightly, cook for about 5 minutes or until theyâre golden and crisp. Remove and serve as a large hot cross bun waffle with the maple and Crunchie butter over it.

For the maple and Crunchie butter:Add the butter to a mixing bowl along with the maple syrup and begin creaming together using an electric hand mixer. Once the butter is light and fluffy add the Crunchie chocolate and mix together.

ing: 1.5 to 2 kg (in one piece) venison shoulder
st: Remove the tough outer membrane from the meat. Coat the venison with the buttermilk and marinate for 1â2 days in the fridge. Dry the meat with kitchen paper and discard the buttermilk. Brown the lamb knuckles in the oil in a large, heavy-based saucepan. Remove using a slotted spoon, season with garlic-and-herb seasoning and set aside.

Brown the venison in the same pan, remove and season. Add the remaining ingredients to the saucepan and bring to the boil. Add the browned meat, cover with a tight-fitting lid and simmer gently until the meat is tender and begins to pull away from the bone (3â4 hours), or cover with foil or greaseproof paper and bake one shelf below the middle in a slow oven (160Â°C) also for 3Â½â4 hours. Cool, flake the meat, remove the bones and reserve the pan juices.

To make the sauce, season the onion with green onion seasoning and sautÃ© in fresh oil until soft and golden. Add the wine and vinegar and boil rapidly over a very high heat until only about Â½ cup liquid remains. Add the reserved pan juices and pepper sauce. If there is less than 2Â½â3 cups sauce, add more water. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Add the flaked meat.

Spoon the filling into a large pie dish. Wedge the onion spiked with 4 cloves into the middle of the dish to support the pastry. Cover with a layer of pastry, brush with egg, then decorate with pastry strips, also brushed with egg. (It will freeze well up to this stage). Bake at 200Â°C for 45 minutes. A frozen pie must be left to thaw, covered with clingfilm, to prevent moisture on the pastry. Bake for 10 minutes longer if still cold when it goes into the oven.

ing: 200 g dark chocolate, chopped and melted
1 Tbsp cocoa powder, plus extra for dusting
st: To make the lemon curd, place a saucepan over a medium to low heat. Whisk together the eggs and egg yolk and place in the saucepan. Add the sugar, butter, lemon juice and zest. Whisk continually for 10â15 minutes, or until smooth and thick. Remove from the heat. Allow to cool and thicken further. Spoon 1 T lemon curd into 6 cavities of an ice tray and freeze.
Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Grease 6 metal dariole moulds or tea cups and dust with cocoa powder. Melt the chocolate and butter in a glass bowl over a pan of simmering water. Cool for 10 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until creamy. Stir in the vanilla extract and the chocolate mixture. Sift in the flour and cocoa and fold in.

Half-fill the moulds with batter, then add a cube of frozen lemon curd to each mould and add more batter until they are two-thirds full. Bake for 15â20 minutes, or until the tops spring back when gently touched. Run a knife around the edges of the cakes and turn out onto plates.WINE:Woolworths Spier Natural Sweet White 2016

t: Hummus, Falafel and Pita Crouton Salad
st: Sign in/Register

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Fresh coriander, chopped, plus extra leaves for garnishing
st: Melt the butter in a medium non-stick pan.
Add the onion and cook over a medium heat until soft and translucent.
Add the eggs and stir continually to scramble.

A few seconds before they are soft scrambled â while still slightly runny â add salt, pepper, chopped coriander and tomatoes, trying to leave most of the tomato juices behind on the cutting board.
Stir through just until tomatoes are warmed.

ing: 1 pineapple, skin and core removed, then roughly chopped
st: 3/4 cup vodka
2 cups iced tea
A coffee machine
A stainless steel jug
A coffee cup

ing: 10 large fresh basil leaves, finely chopped
1 sweet red pepper, very finely chopped
st: In a pan over a medium to low heat, heat the olive oil and gently fry the onion until soft and golden. Add the garlic and cook for another minute. Transfer to a mixing bowl and allow to cool.
Add the remaining ingredients (except the canola oil, ciabatta and Chianti) to the onion-garlic mixture and mix well by hand. Chill for 1 hour, then, using your hands, roll into 50 g balls.
In a large pan over a medium heat, heat the canola oil and, when hot, fry the meatballs (taking care not to overcrowd the pan) until evenly browned.
Transfer the meatballs to a saucepan containing 1.2 litres of gently simmering Napoletana sauce and cook for 12 minutes. Serve immediately with ciabatta and a glass of Chianti.

ing: 2 tbsps finely chopped peanuts or cashews
st: Soften the spring onions, grated onion and minced garlic in butter and 2 tbsps olive oil over a low heat until translucent. Add 1 litre water and 1â2 sticks vegetable stock concentrate and bring to the boil.

Add broccoli florets and baby spinach and cook for 2â3 minutes. Season to taste. Remove from the heat and blend until smooth. Pour into a clean saucepan and bring to a slow simmer. Stir in the juice of Â½ lemon, adding more to taste if you like. Serve warm with a generous swirl of plain yoghurt, fresh mint and sprinkle with dukkah. Serve with the sweet potato chips.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
lemon or lime wedges, for squeezing
st: Spread one side of the bread with the sour cream-and-chive dip, then top with cucumber and season to taste.
Cut the trout to the size of the bread and place half on the sandwiches, reserving the remaining trout. Top the sandwiches with the remaining slices of bread.

Spread a thin layer of sour cream dip over the tops of the sandwiches and arrange the remaining trout on top of the sandwiches. Carefully slice in half using a serrated knife to make finger sandwiches. Sprinkle with chives and serve with the lemon or lime wedges.
Sign in/Register

ing: 2 large carrots,peeled and sliced into 2mm thick ribbons
st: Using a small, heart-shaped cookie-cutter, press out hearts from the beetroot and carrot. Keep separate, wrapped in plastic film.
On a platter, combine the sprouts, fennel, sugar snaps, raspberries and mint. Cover with plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator. This can be prepared a day in advance.
Using a vegetable peeler, peel shards of chocolate.
Top the salad with the beetroot and carrot hearts. Garnish with chocolate shards and drizzle with balsamic blaze.
Eat from one bowl, using chopsticks or forks.

ing: 6 leaves gelatine, soaked in cold water
st: To make the jelly, heat 1 cup wine and the sugar in a saucepan over a medium heat, whisking until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from heat and whisk in the gelatine leaves until dissolved. Whisk in the remaining wine.
Divide the jelly mixture between 4 glasses, filling each glass halfway. Chill until set. Set aside the remaining jelly.
To make the panna cotta, heat the milk, cream, vanilla and sugar in a saucepan over a medium heat. Whisk until the sugar has dissolved, then whisk in the gelatine. Allow to cool.
Once the jelly has set, place the raspberries on the jelly in a single layer, then pour over the cooled panna cotta. Chill to set.
Once the panna cotta has set, pour a thin layer of the remaining jelly over the top. Chill to set once again and serve.
Baste a leg of lamb with a mixture of 4 T ghee and 3 T Woolworths meat masala, then roast uncovered at 170Â°C for 2 hours.
Heat 2 T ghee in a pan over a medium heat, then add 3 cans butter beans and fry for 5 minutes. Add Â½ cup cream and cook for a further 10 minutes. Mash until the desired consistency is achieved.
Heat 2 T ghee in a separate pan, then add 1 T crushed garlic and fry until golden. Add 2 cans cannellini beans and heat. Toss through 1 tub Woolworths basil pesto.
Serve the lamb with the bean mash, fried beans and Woolworths pickled red onions.
Prepare 2 Woolworths gluten-free vanilla cakes according to package instructions. Use one box per cake tin and add the zest of 1/2 lemon to each batch before baking.
To make the icing, beat 500 g full-cream cream cheese. Gradually add 50 g sifted icing sugar, 2 t rose-water, 1 t pink food colouring and the zest of 1 lemon.
Once the cakes have cooled, decorate with the rose cream cheese icing.
Top with chopped pistachios, Turkish delight and edible flowers.
Melt 1 T ghee in a pan over a low heat. Add 4 grated carrots, 125 g desiccated coconut, Â½ t cardamom powder and 1 can condensed milk. Cook until sticky, about 20 minutes.
Melt 200 g 70% dark chocolate. Pour 1 T chocolate into each cavity of a silicone cupcake tray, then top each with 3 T carrot mixture and another 1 T melted dark chocolate. Chill to set.

ing: 18 Small lamb cutlets, brushed with olive oil and seasoned
300 g Basmati rice, rinsed in cold water
st: To make the pilaf, heat the oil in a medium saucepan.
Add the onion and cook for 3 â 4 minutes or until lightly browned.
Add the spices and cook for another 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the rice, coat it well in the oil and spice mixture and cook for a few seconds or until slightly translucent.
Add the vegetable or chicken stock and coconut milk and bring to the boil.
Cover the pot and reduce the heat to a gentle simmer. Leave to cook for a further 12 â 15 minutes or until the rice is tender.
Remove from the heat and add the pistachios, desiccated coconut, mint, coriander and a squeeze of lime to the rice. Season to taste and set aside with the lid on.
Heat the grill to high and cook the lamb cutlets for a few minutes on each side.
Serve the pilaf with the lamb cutlets and lime wedges.

st: Sign in/Register

ing: 2 garlic cloves, finely grated or crushed
4 beef stock, or enough to cover
st: Prepare moderate coals in a Weber. Mix the flour with the spices, herbs and seasoning. Toss the lamb neck in the spice mixture. Heat the oil in a large potjie in the Weber. Brown the meat all over, ensuring the coals do not touch the bottom of the potjie.
Add the onion, garlic, green pepper and leeks and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and canned tomatoes, stir and cook for 5 minutes. Add the beef stock and bring to the boil.
Simmer for 50 minutes, or until soft and cooked through. Add the carrots and onions and cook for a further 5 minutes.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Heat a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add 15 ml olive oil to the saucepan.
Season the beef shin well with salt and pepper.
Sear until nicely browned on all sides, about 15 minutes total.
Remove it from the pot, discard the oil, and return the shin to the pot.
Add 4 cloves crushed garlic.

ing: Free range chicken mini breast fillets
st: Heat a large saucepan over medium heat. Add 15 ml olive oil and 4 cloves crushed garlic, and fry gently for a minute.

ing: 8 free-range chicken thighs (bone in and skin on)
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Grease a 33 cm baking dish. Arrange the potatoes in a layer at the bottom of the dish, adding garlic and some rosemary to each layer, then season. Repeat until the dish is three-quarters full.
Mix the chicken stock with 1â2 cups hot water and pour over the potatoes, but donât cover them.

Stuff the butter, lemon zest and remaining rosemary under the skin of the chicken thighs and generously salt the skin so it will crisp up nicely. Nestle the chicken on top of the potatoes and drizzle with the olive oil. Bake for 40â45 minutes, or until golden brown and the potatoes are cooked through.

ing: 800 g pork steaks, cut into 16 medallions
st: In a medium saucepan, bring the coconut milk, fish sauce, soya sauce, sugar, salt, pepper, curry powder and turmeric to a boil, stirring occasionally.
Reduce the heat and simmer for about 10 â 15 minutes.
Transfer the sauce to a large bowl and allow to cool, then stir in the condensed milk. Season with salt and white pepper.
Add the pork medallions to the sauce and toss, massaging the meat with your hands. Cover and chill for 1 hour.
Prepare the grill on a medium to high heat.
Drain the pork and thread the medallions onto the skewers.
Cook the pork skewers on the braai or under a grill for about 5 â 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until lightly charred and cooked through.
Serve with nut and seed sprinkle and our roasted cherry tomatoes on the tomato soup.
Serve the broccoli soup with crispy kale and crispy onions
Serve the lentil soup with cheesy croutons
Serve the chicken soup with herby croutons and fried garlic and toasted cheese olive ciabatta and mozzarella.
Heat creamy chicken or beef lasagne as per packaging instructions.
Serve with green veg medley and heated olive ciabatta.
Cut the chicken into 4 pieces.
Mix the remaining ingredients except the oil and marinate the chicken for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over a medium to high heat and brown the chicken.
Finish in the oven until cooked through and golden, basting with the citrus marinade.

ing: 1 kg Free range leg of lamb chops
800 g whole peeled tomatoes in tomato juice
Roma tomatoes, roasted slowly over the fire with olive oil and seasoning (optional)
st: To prepare the tagine, season the lamb chops with the Moroccan seasoning and the olive oil, heat up a large potjie pot on the fire, brown the lamb chops, add the onions and cook for 5 minutes
Add the garlic and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, sofritto, stock and water, cook for another 5-10 minutes and season.
To prepare the mealie risotto, fry the leeks and garlic in the olive oil, add rice and vegetable stock, cook like risotto over the fire, add the Parmesan and seasoning when you're ready to serve.
Prepare the breadas per packaging instructions, heat up a pan on the fire, toast the cumin, add the butter and honey, once the bread is baked pour the butter over the bread.
Add the roasted tomatoes and the parsley to the lamb tagine and serve with mealie rice and pot bread.

ing: freeze dried figs, cherries and blueberries
st: Combine the sugar and honey in a pot or high sided pan and place on medium heat. Slowly begin to melt until all the sugar has dissolved. Once the sugar turns a dark amber colour, add the butter, a knob at a time â allow the butter to dissolve in the caramel before adding the next one. When all the butter has been added, pour in the cream and stir.

Continue cooking until the caramel reaches a spreadable texture. To test this, place a teaspoon or tablespoon with the mixture in cold water. Wait a few seconds to cool it down before running your finger through it. If it holds its shape, the caramel is done.
Pour the caramel into a heat-proof bowl and cool completely â you can place it in the fridge to speed the process up.

For the chocolate cups, place a bowl over a pot of simmering water â be sure that the top bowl is not touching the water. Break the chocolate into pieces and place in the bowl, stirring regularly until it melts.

Once perfectly smooth and melted, remove the bowl from the heat and stir to cool down the chocolate, about 1 minute will do. Add 1 tablespoon of the chocolate to a small baking case (small cupcake wrapper) and gently swirl to create a lip up the sides. Do this with 10 of the cases.

Place in the fridge for 5 minutes to set before spooning in Â½ a teaspoon of the caramel, followed by another tablespoon of the melted chocolate to encase the caramel. If the chocolate needs to be melted again simply place it over the simmering water for a few minutes or pop the bowl into the microwave for a few seconds.

While the chocolate in the wrapper is still soft, top with a few pieces of dried fruit, or use flaked salt or toasted sesame seeds. Place in the fridge to set for 5â10 minutes. You can either serve the chocolate cups in the wrappers or remove them before serving.

ing: Olive oil, to fry the garlic and chilli
st: Preheat oven to 180Â°C. Once hot, bake the sausages for 20 minutes until golden.
In a large saucepan over a medium heat sautÃ© the garlic and chilli, add the tinned tomatoes and reduce slightly. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Place the sausages in the sauce, scatter with the drained beans and top with the sliced mozzarella. Place in the oven for 20 minutes until bubbly and golden.

ing: 6 T freshly squeezed lemon juice and zest
st: Preheat the oven to 160Â°C and grease a 24 cm loose-bottomed cake tin with butter.
Process the ginger biscuits until fine, then add the melted butter. Pulse until the crumbs start to stick together.
Use a silicone scraper to line the base and sides of the tin with the crumbs, pushing the crumbs right to the top edge of the tin. Chill until needed.
To make the filling, beat the cream cheese, sour cream, condensed milk and lemon juice and zest until smooth. Add the eggs and mix through. Chill for 1 hour.
Pour the mixture into the crust and spread evenly. Bake for 1 hour in the centre of the oven. Turn the oven off, open the door and allow to cool in the oven.

t: Kitchen Craft Ep 42 Gin fizz cocktails
ing: 60ml (double shot) Abstinence Blood Orange Bittersweet Non-Alcoholic Aperitif
Chilled Villiera MCC Brut, to top
st: For the candied citrus slices, give each slice a coating in the sugar. Shake off any excess sugar and arrange them on a baking tray lined with baking paper. Cover with another sheet of baking paper and a second baking tray to add some weight to the slices.

Place in an oven preheated to 120Â°C to cook for 15 minutes. Remove from the oven, remove the top sheet and the baking paper. Reduce the heat to 75Â°C. Gently dab the slices of citrus with a clean cloth or kitchen paper to remove any excess moisture. Place the tray back in the oven to dry out 1 hour and 45 minutes to 2 hours, until the slices are dry and firm.
Remove from the baking paper and allow to cool. Store in a jar to use in drinks or as a garnish.

For the cocktail, fill a large glass with ice. Add the gin and the aperitif, stir for about a minute with the ice to let some of the ice melt and start to frost the drink. Strain into 2 coupe-style champagne glasses, top with MCC* and garnish with candied citrus slice.

t: Kitchen Craft Ep 43 Gammon with Chipotle
ing: 2 stalks of celery, cut into chunks
130g Whole Chipotle Chillies in Adobo Sauce
The juice of 2 x 440 g pineapple tins, with the rings reserved to garnish
st: To a very large pot, add the onions, carrots, celery, bay leaves and peppercorns. If your gammon was frozen ensure its completely thawed before adding it to the pot. Top with enough water to cover all the ingredients.
Cook the gammon in the pot over medium heat on the stove â it will need to cook 30 minutes for every 500 g, just simmering over medium heat.
Preheat your oven to 200Â°C.

Once cooked, remove the gammon from the pot and cool until it can be handled without burning your hands and fingers. Carefully separate the skin from the fat cap. Score the fat in a diamond pattern with a sharp knife. Place the gammon in the oven to begin rendering out the fat and browning it.
While the gammon is in the oven, prepare your glaze by combining the chipotle, pineapple syrup and spring onions. Blend until smooth.

Remove the gammon from the oven and pour over half the glaze. Be sure that every inch of the gammon, especially the fat, is covered. Return to the oven for 10 minutes or until the glaze has reduced. Remove from the oven, coat in another layer of the glaze and repeat the process to reduce for a further 10 minutes in the oven.
With your gammon well glazed, place the pineapple rings onto the gammon. Fill the centres of the rings with the cherries. Return to the oven and grill for 15 minutes.
Remove from the oven and cool slightly before carving and serving.

Line 2 large cereal bowls with plastic wrap. Add a few scoops of ice cream to the base of the bowl. Smooth out to form a level base using an offset spatula or a spoon. (To help your spoon or spatula not stick to the ice cream you can dip it in hot water for a few seconds.)

Cut slices of the Swiss roll and layer over the ice cream. Repeat the process, alternating with ice cream and Swiss roll, to finish with a layer of ice cream. Place in the fridge to set for 6 hours or overnight.
Prepare the meringue by beating the egg whites until soft peaks form, gradually adding the sugar as you go until all the sugar is added and the whites are smooth and glossy.

Remove the ice cream bombs from the fridge and remove from the bowl by gripping the plastic and slowly pulling it out. Remove the plastic and place the first layer on a serving dish. Do the same to the second bowl and stack on top of the first layer to create an ice cream tower.
Using a spatula, spread the meringue in a thick layer over the ice cream tower. Be sure to cover the tower completely with meringue.

For the scorched effect, caramelise the meringue layer with a blowtorch. Alternatively, heat the vodka in a saucepan over medium heat until just simmering. Light the vodka and pour the flaming spirit over the baked Alaska for a very theatrical dessert.
Decorate with Chuckles rolled in edible gold glitter.

ing: 1 ripe avocado, peeled, pitted and sliced
Â¾ cup Woolies Asian Sweet Indonesian Soy Sauce
Â¼ cup Woolies Asian Rice Vinegar
st: Add the avocado to a blender along with the parsley, mint and basil.

Add the lemon juice, followed by the garlic and green chilli. Season with salt and blend until smooth. If the dressing is thicker than youâd like, simply add a few tablespoons of water at a time until youâve reached the desired consistency. Check the seasoning and serve.

t: Kitchen Craft Ep 47 Oat Bran Muffins
st: Combine the oat bran, cake flour, brown sugar and mixed spice in a large mixing bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix the bicarbonate of soda and milk. Add the oil and eggs and mix well. Pour into the dry ingredients to form a thick batter.
Place the mixture in a container with a tight-fitting lid and refrigerate overnight or for 6 hours.

Heat the oven to 180Â°C. Grease a muffin/cupcake baking tray with butter or non-stick cooking spray. Spoon in the batter. Add the cranberries and swirl into the batter. Sprinkle over some oats. Bake for 15 minutes or until a cake tester comes out clean.

ing: 1 cup full cream long life milk
freshly dried lavender leaves or flowers
st: In a large deep bowl, beat the eggs with the castor sugar well,until fully emulsified.
Add the milk, oil, melted butter (cooled),lavender extract and beat further until foamy.
Sieve all the dry ingredients together and slowly incorporate into the wet ingredients.
Using a large spatula, mix gently until a creamy smooth, lump- free batter forms.
(*Cook's Note: Be careful not to over mix your batter.)
Now gently fold in the dried lavender leaves or flowers.
(Cook's Note: Finely crush the lavender leaves or flowers to release a stronger more potent scent and flavour.)
Gently pour cake batter into a stoneware baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Ensure that you tap the cake tray on a hard surface to release any air bubbles.
Bake in a pre-heated oven at 180Â°C for approximately 55-minutes to 1 hour.
Check to see if the cake is fully cooked through using a skewer.
Allow the cake to cool thoroughly before serving.
Slice and serve on its own.
A delicious fragrantly scented tea-time cake.

ing: 125 g castor sugar, plus 2 T extra for the strawberries
400 ml Woolworths Double Cream Plain Yoghurt
400 g Flavourburstâ¢ strawberries, some halved, some quartered and diced
st: Add a quarter cup of water to a small bowl and add the gelatine. Stir to dissolve and allow to bloom for about 5 minutes.
In the meantime, heat the cream over medium heat with the vanilla and sugar, dissolving the sugar and bringing to a simmer.

Turn off the heat and add the gelatine and the yoghurt. Stir to combine and then add to a jug or beaker with a spout. Whisk any remaining lumps of yoghurt into the mixture until you have a smooth texture. Pour into large espresso-sized cups or ramekins.
Place the espresso cups in the fridge to set for 6 hours or overnight.
Coat the strawberries in the sugar and set aside for 10 minutes.
Once the panna cotta has set you can serve it in the cups or turn it out by quickly submerging the cups halfway in warm water to loosen before turning onto a serving dish.
Top the panna cotta with the strawberries. Drizzle with the strawberry sauce that has formed, crumble over the freeze-dried strawberries, garnish with mint and enjoy.

ing: 2 leeks, halved, then cut into chunks
300 g Woolworths Freshly Frozen Peas, Baby Carrots and Corn
1 rotisserie chicken, meat removed from the bone in chunks (the skin can also be added if you like)
2 x 250 g Woolworths Frozen All Butter Puff Pastry, thawed (to make 2 pies, youâll need 4 x 250 g sheets)
st: To make the bÃ©chamel, place the butter in a saucepan over a medium heat and gently melt. Add the flour and stir for 1 minute, or until the mixture begins to smell slightly nutty.
Gradually add the milk, stirring or using a silicone whisk to incorporate the milk to form a paste. The sauce will become thinner and smooth as you continue stirring and once the milk is added.
Once you have a smooth, silky sauce, place a piece of clingwrap directly on the sauce while you prepare the filling. If any lumps form, blend using a stick blender until smooth.

To make the filling, heat the butter in a pan over a medium heat. Add the leeks and some salt to season and soften them. Cook until the leeks are softened but not brown. Stir in the frozen vegetable mix and cook for about 5 minutes with the lid on, until the carrots have thawed.
Combine the vegetables, chicken pieces and bÃ©chamel sauce in a large bowl and allow to cool to room temperature.

Roll out 1 pastry sheet, making it large enough to fill the bottom and go slightly over the edges of a 24 cm pie dish. Fill the pastry-lined dish with a generous amount of filling. (If youâre only making one pie, the remaining filling can be frozen in a freezer bag.)
Roll out the second sheet of pastry and cover the pie. Cutt off the excess pastry hanging over the edge of the dish but leave enough to crimp the bottom and top layer of pastry together.
Pinch the layers of pastry together with your thumb and index finger, then fold over to seal.
Brush the pie with the beaten egg, then make a small hole in the centre to allow the steam to escape during baking. Sprinkle with the sesame seeds if using.

Place the pie in the fridge and preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Once your oven reaches temperature, place the pie on the lowest shelf in the oven to allow the base of the pie to cook, as well as the top. Bake for 30 minutes until golden and puffed up. Allow to cool slightly before serving.

ing: 70 g Pitted Black Kalamata Olives with a hint of herbs
Radishes and pomegranate rubies, to garnish
1 bottle WCC Brut RosÃ©, to serve
st: Mix and match your favourite treats to make a bounty of beautiful snacks this Valentineâs day, enjoy the last of the summer sun rays in a lush park or on the warm boulders next to the ocean!

ing: 4 T brown sugar, plus extra for sprinkling
1 x 225 g jar Woolworths apple sauce
500 g Woolworths frozen puff pastry sheets, thawed
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Grease a 30 cm fluted or unfluted pie dish. Semi-thaw the puff pastry (itâs best to work with it while semi-frozen) and, using a rolling pin, roll the pastry until it is 35 cm in length. Cut into strips 3.5 cm wide. You will need 12â14 strips. Chill in the fridge while you prepare the apples.
Quarter the apples, remove the cores, then halve each quarter. Place in a large bowl and add the sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice and zest and vanilla seeds. Mix to coat.
Add the apple sauce and mix. Pour the filling into the prepared pie dish.
Place the pastry on top of the filling in a lattice pattern and brush with the egg white. Sprinkle with more brown sugar and bake for 45â60 minutes until golden and bubbling .

When the pie comes out the oven, make the honey caramel. Place the honey in a small saucepan over a medium heat. Once bubbling and dark amber in colour, add the butter. Stir using a rubber spatula. Pour over the warm pie and serve with whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.

ing: 300 g leeks, washed and roughly chopped
Woolworths Garlic Butter-filled Ciabatta, heated, for serving
st: Heat the butter and olive oil in a pan over a medium heat, then add the leeks.
Cook the leeks until soft but not caramelised.
Add themusselsand stir through, coating the mussels in the leeks and butter.
Cover with a lid and steam for 5 minutes. Once most of the mussels have opened, at about 7 minutes, pour in the cream and cook for a further 3 minutes. Discard any mussels that donât open.
Serve the mussels with the ciabatta, garnished with parsley.

t: Kitchen Craft 53: Stuffed Leg of Lamb
ing: 3.5 kg leg of lamb, more or less, butterflied
Â¼ cup extra virgin olive oil, plus extra to drizzle
Freshly ground black pepper and salt
150 g Woolies Sheep & Goatâs Milk Feta PDO cheese
6 cloves of garlic, finely chopped or grated
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. For the stuffing: In a large bowl, combine the parsley, mint, anchovy paste,pistachiosand garlic. Crumble in the feta and combine with the breadcrumbs and a light seasoning of salt. Add a generous amount of pepper before mixing it all with the olive oil.

Lightly season the inside (flesh side) of theleg of lamb, with the fat cap of the lamb facing your work surface. Add the stuffing and press down gently. Layer the pancetta over the stuffing, then fold in the shank of the leg first and then roll up the lamb. Secure with butcherâs twine.
Insert a few sprigs of rosemary between the string and the lamb and drizzle with olive oil to finish.
Place in the oven and roast for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours or until it reaches an internal temperature of 65Â°C or 70Â°C for a more well-done roast.
Allow the lamb to rest for 15 minutes before removing the twine and carving. Serve with lemony green beans, roast potatoes and a salad.

ing: 1 x 250 g pack Parmigiano Reggiano Heart Shaped Pasta
Zest of 1 lemon and lemon to squeeze over
Woolworths Frozen Petits Pois Peas, to serve
1 x 60g tub Woolworths Grated Parmigiano Reggiano
st: Cook the pasta according to the package instructions.
Fry the garlic in butter or olive oil until golden, then add the cream, a handful of the grated cheese, and season to taste.
Meanwhile, fry the pancetta until crispy. Instead of pancetta, you could also add smoked flaked trout orHot Smoked Norwegian Trout bites, warmed to package instructions.
Add the cooked pasta to the creamy sauce and stir through.
Dish the pasta onto a plate and top with steamed petit pois and pancetta bits or flaked trout. Sprinkle with lemon zest, add a splash of lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil and enjoy!

t: Irish coffee is having a moment
ing: 2 cups of your favourite Woolies coffee (like Kenyan single origin 100% Arabica, single origin Costa Rican or Single origin Kilimanjaro)
4 t brown sugar (more or less, depending on how sweet youâd prefer your drink)
st: Prepare your coffee using a Moka pot or French press. Adjust the strength of the coffee by adding more or less coffee grounds.

While your coffee is brewing, prepare your cream by adding chilled cream to a bowl and combining with the vanilla paste. Gently whisk, just until the foam is thick enough to coat a spoon when dipped into the cream. The cream still needs to be pourable.
Pour the coffee into a mug or heat-proof glass and stir in your desired amount of sugar. Add the whiskey and stir.

Pour the vanilla-whipped cream over the back of a teaspoon or large spoon (this helps you to create 2 layers in the drink). Dust with cocoa if you like and serve immediately as an after-dinner drink or wintery cocktail.

ing: Â½ cup Woolworths French Style Mayonnaise
1 kg Woolworths Bulk Classic Potato Salad
st: Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes until cooked but not mushy. Allow to cool and remove the skins
Cut each potato into 3 pieces and set aside.
Combine the mayonnaise, condensed milk, mustard powder and onions and pour over the potatoes. Garnish with the radishes and microgreens.

ing: 2 large free range eggs, at room temperature
edible rose petals or other flowers, to decorate
a drop of pink gel food colouring (optional)
st: 375 g flour
125 g semolina
1 1/2 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp salt
1 tsp ground cardamom
1/2 tsp freshly ground nutmeg
300 g caster sugar
1/2 cup ghee
2 large free range eggs, at room temperature
1 tsp vanilla extract
1/2 cup buttermilk or plain yoghurt
edible rose petals or other flowers, to decorate
200 g mascarpone, whipped, for serving
Drain the beans  and mix with the pesto.
Heat the lasagne according to package instructions and serve with the beans and salad.

ing: 150 g Italian Gorgonzola Semi Soft Medium Fat Cheese
Whole Nocellara Di Castelvetrano Olives in Brine
st: Arrange 1 x 350 g packet antipasto platter on a board and serve with 1 x 100 g packet olive oil bread sticks or 1 x 150 g tomato and oregano bruschetta and 1 x 150 g Gorgonzola.
Add a selection of olives, mini cucumbers and sliced pear and some dips.

ing: 1 T Mediterranean Extra Virgin Olive Oil
3 cups  Organic Liquid Chicken Stock, warmed
2 T Plain Full Fat Cream Cheese
Fresh chives. a handful, finely chopped, to garnish
st: Heat the olive oil in a large pan and saute the mushrooms over medium heat until softened. Remove from the pan and set aside.
In the same pan, melt the butter and cook the onion until softened. Stir in the rice and cook until the rice is lightly toasted.
Add the wine and cook until evaporated, while stirring. Add the stock Â½ cup at a time, stirring until absorbed after each addition. Continue until all the stock is added and rice is cooked al dente.

Stir in the mushrooms and season to taste with the garlic & herb grind. Finish off with the cream and cream cheese, then the grated Parmesan cheese. You can also add a knob of butter to emulsify the risotto further and add a little shine. Garnish with chopped chives before serving.
Preheat the oven to 200Â° C and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Lay the salmon skin side down on the baking paper, lay the sliced butter over the salmon, and then lay the lemon slices over the butter, to completely cover the salmon, slightly overlapping them.
Season with salt and pepper and roast for 15 minutes or until cooked to preferred doneness.

To make the aioli, place the egg yolks, mustard, lemon juice and crushed garlic in a mixing bowl and slowly drizzle in the oil until thick and creamy. Finely chop the dill and mix half into the aioli, use the other half to garnish over the salmon.
Fry off the capers in the sunflower oil until golden brown and crispy and serve over the salmon.

ing: 2 punnets Baby brinjals, sliced in half
st: In an oven proof pan, fry the aubergines in the olive oil cut side down until golden brown.
Add in the harissa and coat over the aubergines.
Roast in an 180 C oven for 15-20 or until cooked.
To make the pesto, add all the ingredients to a blender with half the oil, and blend until a fine paste. Add the rest of the oil and blend until smooth.
For the dukkha mix all the ingredients together, serve over the roasted aubergines, and pesto.
